item.title: Burnley sack head coach Nicky Hayen after 14 games
item.description: Burnley sack head coach Nicky Hayen after 14 games Burnley have sacked Nicky Hayen as head coach after a disastrous start to the 2026-27 season. The Clarets announced the decision just hours after Saturday’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln City. The club released the following statement that read : “Burnley Football Club has dismissed Head Coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.” Hayen was appointed in July to succeed Scott Parker, who left the club at the end of April just days after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed. The 46-year-old won the Belgian title with Club Brugge in 2024. He was tasked with leading Burnley back to the English top-flight but lasted only 14 games in charge. The Clarets held West Ham United to a promising draw on the opening weekend, but then endured a miserable run of form. West Bromwich Albion, Norwich City, Bristol City and Swansea City all took maximum points at their expense. Burnley claimed their first win of the season against Watford on their return from the international break. But they subsequently drew to Charlton Athletic and lost to Wolverhampton Wanderers. The defeat at Lincoln proved to be the final straw for Hayen as the Lancashire club decided to end their association. Burnley are currently 22nd in the Championship table , having collected just eight points from 12 games. They have the joint-worst defensive record in the division alongside Preston North End, conceding 25 goals in 12 matches.

item.title: Why Kirk Herbstreit went off on Arch Manning’s ‘poor decision’ during win against Ole Miss
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images Kirk Herbstreit was on the call for the Texas Longhorns’ dramatic win over the Ole Miss Rebels, and didn’t exactly appreciate Arch Manning’s decision-making. Manning made what proved to be the last touchdown of the game to seal an all-important win against the seventh-best team in the country coming into the weekend. However, there were moments earlier in the game when Manning’s decision-making was being questioned, including by the commentators. Kirk Herbstreit calls out Arch Manning for ‘just hoping’ with poor pass that led to interception During the fourth quarter, with the score tied 24-24, Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns were trying to get past their own 35-yard line. On a first down, with no pressure on him, Manning threw a long pass that got picked by Jalyn Crawford, giving Ole Miss the chance to take the lead. During the broadcast, ESPN commentator Kirk Herbstreit questioned Arch Manning’s decision-making, suggesting that the quarterback didn’t make the best pass. Herbstreit said: “Where is he putting it? This one just didn’t make a lot of sense. Throwing it downfield with 2 defenders…” “The safety almost had to call a fair catch it was in the air so long… Just a poor decision by Manning. Putting it up and just hoping.” Luckily for Manning, his pick didn’t lead to Ole Miss scoring, on the other end. He managed to make up for it soon after, scoring a rushing TD to give the Longhorns the lead. Texas managed to extend this lead later with a field goal. And while Ole Miss came close to coming back, the Longhorns managed to earn a huge win. Last night’s game was a perfect example of the strengths that Manning has as a quarterback, but also the areas he needs to improve before he enters the NFL. Read more: ‘You should be panicked’ – Stephen A. Smith worried by what he’s seen from Arch Manning Arch Manning’s bold statement amid rumours of losing Texas’ QB1 spot to backup KJ Lacey Jr. ‘Below average’ – Analyst references Peyton and Eli in scathing attack on Arch Manning

item.title: When is Premier League 'sacking season' - and who should be worried?
item.description: Could Manchester United's Michael Carrick become the first Premier League manager to lose his job this season? [Getty Images] Premier League managers beware. It's the last thing Manchester United boss Michael Carrick will want to read - as pressure piles on his future after Wednesday's Champions League humiliation in Como - but sacking season is just around the corner. He won't be the only one looking anxiously over his shoulder, though. Last season those Premier League managers - or head coaches, as a majority of top-flight bosses are now officially titled - who vacated their roles had been in charge for an average of 310 days. Is 10 months long enough for a coach to implement their vision, sign the players they want and connect with the fanbase? During the course of 2025-26, 11 bosses parted company with their clubs, with only Enzo Maresca's resignation at Chelsea happening of his own accord. So far in this campaign, all 20 remain in situ. But when is the Premier League's 'sacking season'? And who is at risk even at this early stage of proceedings? When do managers get sacked? It doesn't make for good reading for those struggling managers. The most popular months for in-season managerial departures are November and December, with almost a third of all manager exits happening in these two months alone. Over the course of the competition's 34 completed seasons, there is a clear pattern of club boards opting for change around the autumn international breaks, and before Christmas and, crucially, the winter transfer window, which was introduced in England in 2003. Perhaps most ruthlessly of all, Charlton Athletic's Les Reed was dismissed on Christmas Eve in 2006, having won only one of his seven league games in charge, amassing four points. Reed's 40-day tenure was the shortest in Premier League history for almost two decades, until Sam Allardyce took that record in 2022-23 with a 30-day spell at Leeds United that ended in relegation. Ange Postecoglou lasted 39 days with Nottingham Forest last year. Among the high-profile managers to be shown the door in November are Chelsea's Roberto di Matteo in 2012, Mauricio Pochettino at Spurs in 2019 and Manchester United playing legend Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021. Di Matteo had spectacularly guided the Blues to FA Cup and Champions League success as caretaker boss six months earlier, but paid the price for a poor start in the defence of their European title. December has accounted for Jose Mourinho twice. In 2015 he departed reigning league champions Chelsea by mutual consent and in 2018 he was sacked by Manchester United. How long do managers get now? Last season's average tenure of 310 days for departing managers was the second lowest on record in Premier League history. Only 1994-95 was lower, with an average of 154. item.content:encoded: Could Manchester United's Michael Carrick become the first Premier League manager to lose his job this season? [Getty Images] Premier League managers beware. It's the last thing Manchester United boss Michael Carrick will want to read - as pressure piles on his future after Wednesday's Champions League humiliation in Como - but sacking season is just around the corner. He won't be the only one looking anxiously over his shoulder, though. Last season those Premier League managers - or head coaches, as a majority of top-flight bosses are now officially titled - who vacated their roles had been in charge for an average of 310 days. Is 10 months long enough for a coach to implement their vision, sign the players they want and connect with the fanbase? During the course of 2025-26, 11 bosses parted company with their clubs, with only Enzo Maresca's resignation at Chelsea happening of his own accord. So far in this campaign, all 20 remain in situ. But when is the Premier League's 'sacking season'? And who is at risk even at this early stage of proceedings? When do managers get sacked? It doesn't make for good reading for those struggling managers. The most popular months for in-season managerial departures are November and December, with almost a third of all manager exits happening in these two months alone. Over the course of the competition's 34 completed seasons, there is a clear pattern of club boards opting for change around the autumn international breaks, and before Christmas and, crucially, the winter transfer window, which was introduced in England in 2003. Perhaps most ruthlessly of all, Charlton Athletic's Les Reed was dismissed on Christmas Eve in 2006, having won only one of his seven league games in charge, amassing four points. Reed's 40-day tenure was the shortest in Premier League history for almost two decades, until Sam Allardyce took that record in 2022-23 with a 30-day spell at Leeds United that ended in relegation. Ange Postecoglou lasted 39 days with Nottingham Forest last year. Among the high-profile managers to be shown the door in November are Chelsea's Roberto di Matteo in 2012, Mauricio Pochettino at Spurs in 2019 and Manchester United playing legend Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021. Di Matteo had spectacularly guided the Blues to FA Cup and Champions League success as caretaker boss six months earlier, but paid the price for a poor start in the defence of their European title. December has accounted for Jose Mourinho twice. In 2015 he departed reigning league champions Chelsea by mutual consent and in 2018 he was sacked by Manchester United. How long do managers get now? Last season's average tenure of 310 days for departing managers was the second lowest on record in Premier League history. Only 1994-95 was lower, with an average of 154. Over the decades the patience of club owners has ebbed and flowed, with a notable dearth of sackings in 1995-96 and a more recent peak in longevity in 2021-22 that can largely be attributed to the pandemic. Since then, however, that patience seems to be wearing thin, with the average length of managerial reigns steadily plummeting. Postecoglou's brief stint at Forest last autumn was followed by a similarly short spell at Spurs for Igor Tudor, who picked up one point from five league games before being shown the door after 44 days. A record nine clubs entered this season with new permanent managers. Five of them are currently in the bottom half of the Premier League. With the grave financial consequences of relegation – and social media noise seemingly inescapable – clubs are showing no mercy when it comes to making big decisions. Who should be worried? While no top-flight manager has been dismissed this season, there are several who will be looking over their shoulder before November's international break. The scrutiny on Carrick has only intensified after the chastening 4-1 defeat by Como at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. Following Lisandro Martinez's critique of the club's hierarchy last week, club captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick's tactics in Como, suggesting all is not well in the Old Trafford dressing room. Asked about Carrick's future after the coach cut an isolated figure as he applauded the away fans alone at full-time, Match of the Day pundit Nedum Onuoha said: "Bruno Fernandes thinks the tactics were essentially wrong in this game, while Michael Carrick thinks the players weren't running enough for the tactics to work out. "When you find those sorts of splits it can be very hard within a dressing room to maintain that sort of energy behind the manager. "So I think for Carrick himself to go and see those fans... he knows how bad this game was in particular." Tudor's successor at Spurs, Roberto de Zerbi, has eased any pressure on him after successive wins moved them to 12th in the Premier League, while Fulham's Alvaro Arbeloa has also moved the heat away from his future for now with back-to-back 1-0 wins. But new Forest boss Oliver Glasner, and Sunderland's Regis le Bris - whose side are juggling Europa League football - will be feeling a little bit anxious at the moment. Marco Rose, another newcomer to English football, hasn't had the most convincing domestic start with Bournemouth, who face Carrick's United at Old Trafford on Sunday. But surely the midweek win against AC Milan, which extended their perfect Europa League start, is enough to keep the pressure off him for now? Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage apologised to fans after the 5-0 battering by Brighton on Sunday and faces a fight to keep his job only four months after joining from Lens. His side entertain Newcastle on Sunday, another side who's new boss, Matthias Jaissle, could do with a positive result quickly. It may feel early to talk about managers feel the pressure, but history tells us that it might not be long before someone is on their way out. What Man Utd need now is stability, not more changes - Pulis Man Utd not an unmanageable club - Carrick Palace manager Sage facing fight to keep his job

item.title: 'I'm 28 and training to play my third professional sport'
item.description: Jacob Smillie has already played rugby and American football - now he is training as a wrestler [DAVE EDWARDS/BBC] Jacob Smillie is only 28 - yet he has already had a whirlwind career in elite sport. Smillie, from Bradford, has represented Jamaica at rugby union, played professional rugby league, and lived in Germany and Poland after signing for American football teams. In September he made his debut as a professional wrestler. "I've always been a massive fan of wrestling - so for me it was only a matter of time," he said. After studying at Tong High School and Leeds City College, Smillie played rugby union at academy level for Doncaster Knights, and was scouted for the Jamaica national side, qualifying on ancestry. His rugby league clubs include Bradford Bulls and Halifax Panthers, but in 2021 he was asked to try out at the NFL Combine in London when video clips of his speed were spotted. Although he was not selected for the NFL International Player Pathway programme and went undrafted after trying out for the Canadian Football League, Smillie ended up playing for several teams in Europe on a full-time basis. Smillie played American football for clubs in Germany and Poland [FABIAN UEBE] "It was great playing over in Germany and testing myself against top athletes," he said. "It also showed me American football in Europe is massive with the fanbase it has." But he has jumped at the chance to try wrestling, having been a childhood fan and with a number of friends involved in it already. Smillie made his wrestling debut in September [ELEVATION WRESTLING] Smillie travels to Loughborough to train at the Elevation Wrestling Academy with Joseph Conners , an experienced wrestler who has taken part in WWE events. "The way I see it, if you want to be the best, you've got to train with the best," Smillie added. He will now feature in a number of wrestling shows across England. Smillie has trained with wrestlers around the UK, including in Sheffield [PURSUIT PRO WRESTLING] Smillie believes there are plenty of skills he has been able to transfer from his other sports. "You have to be really fit, you've got to be agile and strong," he explained. "One of the differences I would say is you've got to have a good personality and a good character, that's massive in wrestling. "You can be a great wrestler but if you have the character as well, that can help you stand out." According to Conners, "the sky can certainly be the limit" for his new protégé. "One of the big things you can't teach is work ethic and obviously with his background in professional sports, he's got that in abundance. "Not only has he trained with myself, he's also been going up and down the country training with some of the top pros who've done it in the UK over the last 15-20 years, so you can't knock his ambition." Smillie's coach, Joseph Conners, is based in Loughborough [DAVE EDWARDS/BBC] Smillie grew up watching American wrestlers including Dwayne "the Rock" Johnson and Triple H, but in the UK there have been shows at Wembley Stadium, Leeds Arena and Sheffield Arena in recent years. Smillie added: "My goal is to take this as far as I possibly can and ultimately wrestle at the highest level, whether that's WWE, AEW or the top independent promotions." Listen to highlights from West Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North . item.title: It's official, Liverpool have secured their FOURTH £100m star
item.description: It's official, Liverpool have secured their FOURTH £100m star Liverpool have spent a lot of money over the last couple of years. The Reds have spent £100m+ on three occasions. They now have a team full of £100m superstars. Florian Wirtz was the first, followed by Alexander Isak and then Bradley Barcola arrived this summer. There's a sentiment that Liverpool might have overspent. In a market where Rayan Cherki cost £30m, Wirtz for over £100m might not have been the wisest move. However, ultimately Liverpool paid market value for all of these players. The Reds didn't overspend because they knew and they trusted their recruitment and they still have faith that they will be proved right in the long-term. Wirtz, Barcola and Isak have not yet justified their big transfer fees, but in the coming months and years they could easily do so. Liverpool are building an invincible team Wirtz, Barcola and Isak are going to be the future faces of this team. But it's true that their ability to deliver also hinges massively on the team that is being built around them. Right now that team is far from perfect. There are signs and positive improvements. Jeremy Jacquet is likely going to be a future staple at the back. Dominik Szoboszlai could become the Reds' captain in the long-term. And in Trey Nyoni Liverpool also have a phenomenal midfielder who has everything it takes to dictate the tempo and rhythm of the game. Put all of them together and the only area where Liverpool are really lacking is in the full-back roles and in finding the perfect heir to Fabinho's throne. With a proper holding midfielder and a right-back, this Liverpool team could be invincible. Liverpool's fourth £100m player revealed And the reason why Liverpool look so balanced and in such a good place right now is because they don't just have three £100m players. They have four. Rio Ngumoha might not have cost the Reds that much. They got him for practically pennies from Chelsea. However, he is absolutely worth £100m. The England international made it 'official' this week by breaking records set by Lamine Yamal on top of also becoming the second youngest Englishman to debut for the senior national team behind Jude Bellingham. Given the way the market is at the moment. A winger like Ngumoha comes at a premium price and that price is in excess of £100m. Thankfully, the Reds didn't have to spend that much to get him, which is why he might be the best out of the club's entire quartet of £100m players.

item.title: Watch: Lazio March on as Taylor Scores Against Parma – The Highlights
item.description: Watch: Lazio March on as Taylor Scores Against Parma – The Highlights The official Serie A YouTube channel uploaded the highlights from Saturday’s entertaining affair between Lazio and Parma at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. Christos Mandas the Hero in the First Half The two sides traded jabs in a fast-paced first half, beginning with Parma striker David Romero, who drove towards the goal unchallenged, but Christos Mandas stopped the shot with his leg. Davide Frattesi then skipped past Mariano Triolo and stormed to the box, forcing the latter to bring him down, but the referee waved play on. Player Ratings: Lazio 2-1 Parma – Belahyane & Taylor Run The Show Emanuele Valeri then found El Bilal Toure with a clinical cross, but Mandas pulled off an excellent save to deny the visitors once more. At the other end of the pitch, Mattia Zaccagni set up Gustav Isaksen with a delicate cross. The Dane’s header sailed over Edoardo Corvi, but was kept out by the woodwork. The first half ended with another Mandas save on Romero. Kenneth Taylor & Diego Carlos Score for Lazio Swiftly after the break, Lazio found the breakthrough through Kenneth Taylor, who pounced on the second ball, found the right shooting angle, and beat Corvi at his near post with a clever low drive. Ten minutes later, Diego Carlos doubled the hosts’ lead by scoring an own goal after failing to deal with Nuno Tavares’ square ball to the mouth of the goal. Simoni Lontani Nets Fortunate Goal for Parma The Biancocelesti couldn’t add to their lead despite numerous chances, while Parma grabbed one back in bizarre fashion deep into extra time. Simoni Lontani intended to find a teammate’s head with a cross, but instead evaded the crowd, including Mandas, and sneaked past the line after hitting the post. But despite conceding a late goal, Lazio went on to win 2-1 and seize the top spot in the table while waiting for Inter Milan’s game against Fiorentina on Sunday.

item.title: Where to watch Knicks vs. Magic today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Sunday NBA game
item.description: Where to watch Knicks vs. Magic today: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for Sunday NBA game originally appeared on The Sporting News . It's a long season, but the reigning champions didn't expect a 0-2 start. item.title: 3 takeaways from No. 10 Utah’s ‘GameDay’ victory over No. 14 Houston
item.description: Utah Utes wide receiver Creed Whittemore (2) runs with the ball during a game against Houston at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News After going down 10-0 in the third quarter Saturday night against the Houston Cougars, it was time for the Utah Ute offense to turn things on. After a struggle in the first half that included a terribly awry field goal attempt, quarterback Devon Dampier answered the call and marched the offense down the field for a quick touchdown to put Utah on the board, and the Utes ultimately won, 21-13. Dampier finished with 354 total yards and Utah’s defense shined as the Utes now find themselves atop the Big 12 standings on a day in which BYU and Texas Tech both lost their first games of the season. Utah is just one of three undefeated teams remaining in the country, alongside Miami and UCLA. New playbook section unlocked For much of the season, despite some fun variations in the Ute offense, it always seemed there was still something being held back in Utah’s playbook — Dampier’s legs. In the 2025 season, the quarterback rushed for 835 yards, but in 2026, he had only ran for 198 through six games entering Saturday, but perhaps this was his breakout game. 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News In addition to his yardage, he scored two rushing touchdowns. He did throw two interceptions, but he ultimately made the plays needed to help the Utes win. On a night when Wayshawn Parker only ran for 47 yards, the ground game was generated through Dampier. It was not always perfect or easy going for the offense, especially in the first half, but three rushing touchdowns against the Cougars helped Utah get the victory. Utah’s pressure got to Houston Still waiting on a sack from one of its defensive ends, Utah made things difficult for Houston quarterback Conner Weigman and the rest of the Cougar offense, especially in the second half. Pressure on Weigman made it difficult for Houston to get much going, including a big hit by Jackson Bennee late that caused a fumble to put Dampier and company in business inside Houston’s 10. Dampier scored a touchdown on the next play for the game’s final points. The Ute defense stiffened up multiple times to keep the home side in the game. The first came when the Cougars turned it over on downs in the first quarter while they were inside the five instead of opting for a field goal. Utah held the visitors to field goals on two other occasions, only allowing one touchdown on the first drive of the second half that took more than half of the third quarter. While the offense struggled for large stretches, the defense left the team with opportunities. The lone big victory for the Big 12 in a nightmare weekend The Big 12 was riding high after last weekend resulted in three teams from the conference in the top 10 and four in the top 15. But after this weekend the momentum was all but lost, except for one team. As Texas Tech traveled north to Cincinnati

item.title: Enzo Maresca explains Phil Foden substitution as Man City lose midfield battle against Aston Villa
item.description: Aston Villa FC v Manchester City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Enzo Maresca has defended his ruthless half-time substitutions after Manchester City struggled in midfield during their clash with Aston Villa. The manager explained his tactical decision to introduce Phil Foden instead of Ayyoub Bouaddi as City chased an early deficit. Maresca acts ruthlessly again City have rarely fallen behind during Maresca's tenure. However, when the team does trail, the manager has consistently shown a ruthless streak. The Cityzens reacted well to conceding an early goal against Aston Villa on Saturday. Iliman Ndiaye came incredibly close to equalising, but the forward was ultimately denied by the post. Seeking a turnaround, Maresca made a decisive double substitution at the break. Rayan Cherki was sacrificed at half-time, suffering the exact same fate as he did during the recent Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain . Foden chosen over Bouaddi Instead of introducing Bouaddi to shore up the middle, Maresca opted to bring Foden off the bench. Eyebrows were raised when Foden initially missed out on a starting spot following his midweek hat-trick. Maresca defended his tactical alterations when questioned after the match. He drew comparisons with the recent European fixture where City successfully altered the momentum. "I think against PSG it was a bit different," Maresca explained to reporters. "Today we needed a technical midfielder, that's why Rayan was out and Phil was inside." City lose the midfield battle The introduction of a creative midfielder failed to solve City's core problem on the day. The game became frantic and end-to-end, leaving vast amounts of space in the middle of the park. Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez had previously formed a faultless midfield partnership against Manchester United and Liverpool. However, like in the PSG match, they found themselves losing crucial duels against Villa. Despite leaving him on the bench, Maresca backed Bouaddi to feature prominently soon, saying: "No doubt that Ayyoub is going to help us. Today Enzo and Elliot both had a very good game and we have so many games that Ayyoub is going to play minutes." Brighton test awaits next Maresca will need to find the right midfield balance quickly as the fixtures continue to pile up. The manager must decide whether to rotate his established partnership of Anderson and Fernandez. City turn their attention away from the league as they prepare for domestic cup action. The squad will face Brighton in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday.

item.title: 🗞️ Front pages: golden Clásico, Araña's regrets and drama in Valencia
item.description: 🗞️ Front pages: golden Clásico, Araña's regrets and drama in Valencia Sunday’s front pages are devoted to El Clásico, but with one eye, of course, on the Ballon d’Or, whose winner will be announced tomorrow. AS calls it “the big showdown”, Marca and Sport give it the golden treatment, and Mundo Deportivo tones things down, settling for “crucial”. Lamine Yamal and Mbappé face off a day before the Ballon d’Or winner is revealed, and a Barça victory would leave Mourinho’s Madrid nine points behind. The front pages beyond El Clásico Away from El Clásico, Julián Álvarez scores the only goal in a 1-0 win over Depor (with Oblak preventing an equaliser) and apologises “to our fans” for his comments at the World Cup. Atlético move to within two points of the leaders, which is the best way to make sure an apology gets a proper hearing. Racing come from behind to beat Espanyol (2-1), leaving Manolo González hanging by a thread, while at Mestalla, Villarreal win 2-1 thanks to a 95th-minute goal from Mikautadze, sinking Valencia into the relegation zone. "Sir Alex, I need your help" In the Sunday Express, Shearer backs Kane for the Ballon d’Or, while Carrick sends an SOS to Sir Alex with United in freefall. Today’s clash with Bournemouth has all the makings of a drama... This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: UFC 333 Official Scorecard: Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili
item.description: The UFC 333 bantamweight title trilogy between Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili went the distance on Saturday in Abu Dhabi. Yan retained his title defeating Dvalishvili via unanimous decision. All three of their fights ended up in the judges’s hands. All three judges scored the fight the same, 48-47 for Yan. The scorecards were all the same with Dvalishvili winning the first two rounds and Yan earning 10-9s in rounds three, four, and five. Take a look at the official scorecard below. item.title: Vikings Receive Strong Jauan Jennings Message Amid 49ers Speculation
item.description: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty Many see the Minnesota Vikings as a buyer with the Nov. 10 trade deadline looming. Nonetheless, the Vikings could also make moves to bring in draft assets for players who don’t fit their team after a handful of weeks. Minnesota already traded away J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for a Day 3 pick. Could they do so with another player who’s struggled to fit in with the offense, wideout Jauan Jennings? The veteran wideout has had two catches for nine yards in four games this season for Minnesota, per StatMuse . As a result, Jennings has found himself in trade speculation leading up to the deadline. One potential landing spot for the wideout is a return to the San Francisco 49ers, given the team’s injuries at the receiving position and his knowledge of the offensive system. However, Matthew Coller of “Vikings Collective” noted that Minnesota should avoid trading Jennings to the Niners or any team that could potentially hurt them. “I wouldn’t help San Francisco with anything right now,” Coller said in an Oct. 24 video from the “Vikings Collective” YouTube channel . “If I’m the Minnesota Vikings, I don’t care if Jauan Jennings wants to go back to that team or not. You’re going to the AFC if they’re trading him away because that’s where he can’t hurt you, and not to Buffalo because he can hurt you there.” Why Hasn’t Jauan Jennings Worked for Vikings So Far Moreover, Coller went into detail regarding why the Jennings signing hasn’t panned out for the Vikings so far, as the team will need to decide whether to keep him for potential depth. They have experienced injuries at wideout, but he could also be unhappy about not being a key piece on offense. “With Jauan Jennings, it’s been really shocking to see how poorly he’s fit with this offense,” Coller added. “But then, when you think about it deeper, the specifics of the routes for the wide receivers are so detailed with this offense, and Jennings had a loss in his life where he missed the game against Chicago. “My understanding is that impacted him pretty greatly. His time on task, their terminology with the quarterbacks. He was with two different quarterbacks. How often did Jauan Jennings play wide receiver two? Probably not much during training camp, but then all of a sudden, you’re at wide receiver two, or you’re being asked to do that. “It’s been a really difficult ride with a lot of circumstances that we didn’t expect. What they can do here with Jauan Jennings is see two more weeks of whether you fit into the role that we originally signed you for. If you don’t, then it would be time to move on, and that’s why they have Odell Beckham . They could also acquire somebody else if they wanted to.” Panthers Floated as Potential Destination for Jauan Jennings Meanwhile, aside from a potential return to the 49ers, another potential team that would make sense for Jennings is the Carolina Panthers , who might want another pass-catching target for Bryce Young

In an Oct. 22 article , Carolina Panthers on SI’s Mark Livingston floated Jennings as a realistic trade target for the team. “This is probably the one I’m most torn on because I really like what Carolina already has with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker ,” Livingston wrote. “We finally got to see those two together against Philadelphia, and it looked pretty good. “Coker came back with 97 yards while McMillan finished with 86, giving Bryce Young two receivers who can make defenses pay instead of asking McMillan to do everything. I still wouldn’t mind adding Jennings. He’s physical, he’ll block and he’s shown he can be productive when he’s given opportunities.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Vikings Receive Strong Jauan Jennings Message Amid 49ers Speculation appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Barcelona target Julian Alvarez apologises to Atletico Madrid fans after summer controversy: ‘It was a mistake’
item.description: Barcelona target Julian Alvarez apologises to Atletico Madrid fans after summer controversy: ‘It was a mistake’ Julian Alvarez has apologised to Atletico Madrid supporters for his comments about leaving the club for Barcelona during the summer, admitting he understands why fans were angry. The Argentine forward addressed the controversy after scoring the winner in Atletico’s 1-0 La Liga victory over Deportivo La Coruna on Saturday. His goal and subsequent apology could mark an important step towards repairing his relationship with the club’s supporters. Alvarez admits his Barcelona transfer comments were a mistake Alvarez’s future became a major talking point during the summer after he expressed his desire to leave Atletico , with Barcelona reportedly his preferred destination. However, Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin refused to entertain negotiations, leaving the forward to continue in Madrid. The situation contributed to a difficult start to the campaign, with sections of the Atletico support expressing their frustration through boos and jeers. Following his goal against Deportivo, Alvarez chose to address the issue before taking questions. “First of all, I wanted to say a few words; I wanted to apologise to our fans for what I said during the World Cup. “It was a mistake on my part, both in terms of how I said it and the timing, and above all because I understand why people are angry; as a fan myself, I would have been angry too, especially given how they’ve stood by me all this time. “Even in these last few weeks, when they’ve been so generous – I really appreciate that,” he remarked. Alvarez thanks Atletico teammates for their support Alvarez also made it clear that his priority is now improving his performances and helping Atletico compete for major honours. Julian Alvarez has apologised to Atletico Madrid fans. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “Now I have to focus on working hard, on continuing to improve my performance alongside the whole team – whom I’d like to thank because they’ve given me so much throughout this time. “So, let’s get to work; we’ve got some very important things to do with the team.” The forward credited his teammates with helping him through the difficult period and said his recent performances had begun to improve. “As I said just now, I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me so much. They’ve given me so much during this time. “I’m working to improve, and I’ve felt better in recent matches – both physically and on the ball. So, I’ll help the team and give my best,” he concluded.

item.title: Bruins Postgame: James Hagens Is Giving Marco Sturm More Reasons to Trust Him
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins are getting more out of James Hagens than what shows up on the scoresheet. The Bruins (9-2-1) extended their point streak to eight with a 6-4 win over the San Jose Sharks (6-5-1) on Saturday night at TD Garden. Hagens, Casey Mittelstadt , Marat Khusnutdinov , David Pastrnak , Fraser Minten , and Will Borgen all scored, while Jeremy Swayman made 21 saves on the other end of the ice. Also Read: Bruins Score Four in Third, Extend Point Streak to Eight Games Hagens recorded his fourth goal of the season and his NHL career on Saturday night. He buried an Elias Lindholm rebound past Alex Nedeljkovic to give the Bruins a 4-3 lead halfway through the third. Three of Hagens’ four goals have come directly in front of the net, with the other one coming from behind the goal line. “We’re pushing him pretty hard,” head coach Marco Sturm said postgame. “Getting more to the paint, more to the inside is where you score the goals. And so good for him that he realized that, and look at the four goals he scored, right? So, good for him, but just listening and also taking it really seriously, and I’m glad it worked out.” Hagens assisted on the game’s opening goal, good for his second multi-point night in the NHL. He is up to nine points (4-5–9) on the season and is tied for the lead among rookies in both points and goals. The rookie is producing offensively, and his linemate has been just as impressed with what Hagens does to create those opportunities. “As a player, I think obviously you see the skill and the shot definitely stands out to me,” Casey Mittelstadt said of Hagens. “But, I feel like he’s done a heck of a job on the forecheck. I feel like he’s taking pucks away all the time and that’s not easy to do as a young kid.” Hagens has also been making his presence felt in the defensive zone. He did not block a shot on Saturday, but he still leads all forwards in the league with 16 blocked shots, something he said he takes pride in ahead of the game. James Hagens currently leads all NHL forwards with 16 blocked shots. “It’s definitely something that I try to take pride in. James Hagens currently leads all NHL forwards with 16 blocked shots. “It’s definitely something that I try to take pride in. It’s just the d-zone, and when a guy is getting ready to shoot, if that’s your guy, you’re going to make sure that you’re in the shooting lane.” On… pic.twitter.com/Ho2SNUue6u — Jack Studley (@jackstudley13) October 24, 2026 Marco Sturm has shown plenty of trust in the Bruins’ younger players this season, and Saturday night was another example. Sturm sent Elias Lindholm’s line, with Hagens and Mittelstadt, out for the opening faceoff against Ryan Warsofsky’s top line of Macklin Celebrini , Will Smith , and Collin Graf . That was not their only matchup against each other. The Bruins’ third line played over eight minutes against San Jose’s top line at 5-on-5. “Yeah, I thought they did pretty good. Again, it was just a weird game today, a lot of ups and downs. But 5-on-5, I thought it was actually pretty good,” Sturm said. “Celebrini is a special player. He will be a special player; he already is, but he’s just going to grow, and it’s hard to defend him every time he’s on the ice because he wants to be the difference. We need all three of them, pretty much, including our defensive pair, so we need five guys to just be alert. But overall, I thought the guys did a good job, and they got a lot of trust, and they scored a few goals, so good for them.” According to Natural Stat Trick , the Bruins outattempted the Sharks 16-6 and held a 9-4 advantage in shots on goal during Hagens’ 5-on-5 minutes against Celebrini. They also outscored San Jose 2-0 and generated 2.46 expected goals compared to just 0.57 for the Sharks. Hagens said they “had an idea” of the matchup before the game and credited his ability to fall back on his teammates to help him play at his best. Elias Lindholm and his two-way game played a big part in making the matchup work, something Mittelstadt quickly pointed to after the game. “I mean, obviously, [Celebrini’s] a heck of a player. I think we all know that, and he has good players around him as well, but I think a lot of that credit goes to Lindy,” Mittelstadt said postgame. “Lindy does a heck of a job in all three zones. So, you know, me and (Hagens) are there to support him and help him when he needs it. But thankfully, I don’t think he needs it that often.” Also Read: Bruins’ Elias Lindholm Feels Healthy, Sturm Talks ‘Target on His Back’ The matchup was another big responsibility for Hagens, but it was one he handled well. Hagens skated for 9:57 at even strength, with 8:03 of that time against Celebrini and San Jose’s top line. Hagens, 19, was at Boston College last year watching players like Celebrini play in the NHL. One year later, he is keeping them off the scoresheet. “It’s special. It’s a great feeling to be able to be out there and, you know, trying to stop those guys from scoring,” Hagens said. “You want to do your best, and you want to win games, and if that’s your role, then you got to be able to go out there and do it. It’s definitely cool being able to, you know, these players I grew up watching and especially last year, being in college, I was watching these guys. Now you’re out there trying to stop them all night long.” FOLLOW @JACKSTUDLEY13 ON 𝕏 | FOLLOW @BOSHockeyNow ON 𝕏 Related Headlines Bruins Score Four in Third, Extend Point Streak to Eight Games Bruins Postgame: DiPietro’s First Shutout Means So Much More Bruins Roll Past Predators, Extend Point Streak to Seven Games Read more at Boston Hockey Now

item.title: Stoever shuts out Steelers as Devils claim cup win
item.description: Man of the match Christian Stoever saved 31 shots for his second shutout of the season [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils took another step towards the Challenge Cup knockout stages with a tense home win against Group A leaders Sheffield Steelers. Kristoff Kontos scored the game's only goal after 43 seconds of the first period, with Devils' netminder Christian Stoever making a string of outstanding saves to protect the home side's lead. The visitors also struck the pipework twice, while Cardiff's Riley Brandt and Nick Welsh went close. Despite the 1-0 final scoreline, Devils' head coach Paul Thompson described the game as a "classic win". "An absolute battle for 60 minutes, and Sheffield are a very, very good team," he said. "They probably had more offensive zone time against us than any team has had this year, but when they did get inside I thought [Stoever] was outstanding. "Sometimes you've just got to roll your sleeves up and battle, and that's what we did." With two games remaining for Cardiff they lie in third place on 10 points, two behind Sheffield and Nottingham Panthers who both only have one more game to play in the group stage. Devils travel to Nottingham on Sunday, 25 October (16:00 GMT) before their final game at Manchester Storm on Sunday, 1 November. Guildford Flames, in fourth, also have 10 points with a final game at Coventry Blaze this weekend. Their hosts - and Storm - are not completely out of the running for third spot having played fewer games. The top two sides in Group A automatically qualify for the semi-final, with the third-placed team facing an elimination tie against the runners-up in the smaller group B. GB men and women to make history in Glasgow

item.title: 🤔 Angry with the coach?! Füllkrug explains outburst after being subbed
item.description: 🤔 Angry with the coach?! Füllkrug explains outburst after being subbed Niclas Füllkrug enjoyed a pretty successful afternoon yesterday—as he so often has since returning to Bremen. Two goals from the penalty spot took him to the top of the Bundesliga scoring charts, and he got to celebrate his Bremen side’s 3–2 away win in Mainz. One incident, however, left everyone involved confused. The former Germany international was substituted in the 81st minute, with Cedric Itten coming on in his place. On his way to the bench, Füllkrug became visibly upset. He gestured wildly, waved his winter jacket around and shouted a few words over his shoulder towards the coaching staff. Füllkrug explains frustration after substitution Was the striker angry with Daniel Thioune for taking him off? That was pretty clearly the case yesterday with Felix Nmecha, for example, who had to make way for Jobe Bellingham in the 79th minute of the big clash against Eintracht Frankfurt. The Germany star looked seriously annoyed with his coach afterwards. We have seen that explanation for frustration on the touchline plenty of times. But that was not the case with Niclas Füllkrug—quite the opposite. After the final whistle, he told Sky: “No, it was more that I was absolutely exhausted. The more tired you are, the more emotional you get. There’s no malice in it at all, but sometimes that’s just how it is.” 📸 KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV - AFP or licensors Looking back, he would describe the situation as more “funny” than “fiery”, and immediately explained why: “I was completely spent. I was waiting to be substituted because I realised we needed eleven men on the pitch who could really put in the running. And I wanted to come off because, by that point, the game had really started to drain my energy. Defending that deep was very intense, and Mainz weren’t hesitating to put crosses in either.” Füllkrug himself had thought the substitution was being deliberately delayed. That was the reason for his outburst on the touchline. Only afterwards did he realise that the ball probably just hadn’t gone out of play. War of words between Füllkrug & Amiri Not all the emotions had subsided immediately after the final whistle. Fülle was in the spotlight again when he clashed with Germany star Nadiem Amiri. He told DAZN: “Amiri wasn’t being very respectful towards my teammate. So I told him to tone it down.” Amiri also gave his take on the situation to a Sky reporter: “It’s all good. I know Fülle from the national team. A few things in the game had been pissing me off right from the start. After a foul on Danny da Costa, Füllkrug didn’t want to apologise. I was already a bit angry about that. But that’s football. We get along. A few insults were exchanged. But it’s all good, no hard feelings.” ADVERTISEMENT: Should Füllkrug return to the national team? Frank Buschmann and Florian Schmidt-Sommerfeld share their takes on TIPICO’s “Die Ansage”! Jesus Garza got off a right footed shot from outside the area that went wide. Juninho would lob a shot past Tigres goalkeeper, Nahuel Guzman, but the ball went wide. It would eventually reach Uriel Antuna, whose cross was headed just wide by Robert Morales. A great pass by Huerta would be deflected to Morales but his right footed shot would be deflected wide. A cross into the area was volleyed by Huerta but Guzma would easily save it. A longball would force Guzman to clear the ball before Juninho would get to it and go off alone into the area. The cross into the area was headed by Rodrigo Aguirre but right to Navas. The halftime whistle blew and the half ended with both teams creating few chances. The 2nd half started with the team coming out with the same 11 they started the match with. A pass into the area was volleyed wide by Carrasquilla. Huerta got past a defender and got off another “rabona” cross that was deflected by Guzman. A great low cross by Pablo Bennevendo would get past two Tigres’ defenders and Guzman, to reach Robert Morales, who from close range would tap in the ball into the net to score and give Pumas the 1-0 lead. Tigres subbing out Rodrigo Aguirre, Jesus Garza and Cesar Araujo for Guillermo Martinez, Ozziel Herrera and Emiliano Gomez. Brunetta got off a right footed shot from outside the area that went well wide. A cross into the area was deflected into the path of Morales, whose right footed volley would go just wide. A good combination play ended with the ball being left for Juan Brunetta in the area, where he got off a right footed shot past Navas to score and give Tigres the goal that tied the match at 1-1. A ball lowered in the area was headed wide by Antuna. Pumas subbed out Pedro Vite, Pablo Bennevendo and Uriel Antuna for Victor Arteaga, Alvaro Angulo and Alan Medina. Tigres subbed out Diego Lainez for Ricardo Monreal. A cross into the area forced Navas to grab the ball off the feet of Herrera. Tigres subbed out Mauro Lainez for Vladimir Loroña. From outside the area Gomez got off a right footed shot that was saved by Navas. From outside the area, Herrera got off a great right footed shot that forced a great save by Navas. Pumas subbed out Juninho for Santiago Lopez. Off a free kick, the cross into the area was headed by Herrera but Navas made a fantastic save. A counter by Pumas would end with Medina getting off a left footed shot that was saved by Guzman. Pumas subbed out Adalberto Carrasquilla for Israel Luna. Hugo Sanchez’s celebration night, on the 50th anniversary of his Liga MX debut, was the only reason for home fans to celebrate as Pumas got a tie against Tigres in a match they needed to win. Pumas now sits at 17 points and will need a miracle to make it to the Liguilla. This is extremely disappointing for the team that finished in first place during the Clausura 2026 and lost the final. New coach Esteban Solari has failed to find the solution to Pumas’ numerous problems and Saturday night was another chance to see his lackluster work. Pumas now has three mus win matches and one of those is against their biggest rival and current first place in Mexico, Club America. Tigres will travel to Pachuca as they are even close to ending the season without post season games.

item.title: ‘Human error’ contributed to special teams lows for Texas vs. Ole Miss
item.description: BANGKOK, THAILAND - AUGUST 02: A protester dressed in a Harry Potter themed outfit and wielding a wand campaigns for the freedom of Arnon Nampa during a Harry Potter themed protest at Democracy Monument on August 02, 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand. Pro-democracy activists gather at Democracy Monument during a Harry Potter themed protest called "Letter from Azkaban", calling for constitutional reform and expressing solidarity with political prisoners, most notably Arnon Nampa, a human rights lawyer who is still currently detained after receiving his first prison sentence in a lèse-majesté case. This demonstration marked six years since the original Harry Potter-themed protests that became a symbol of Thailand's youth-led democracy movement. (Photo by Mailee Osten-Tan/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Steve Sarkisian doesn’t have a magic wand to fix the special teams issues that consistently plague his Texas Longhorns. Neither does special teams coordinator Jeff Banks, clearly. After No. 19 Texas beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 in Austin on Saturday despite multiple special teams mishaps, once again, including a successful fake punt and successful onside kick by the Rebels, anyone in possession of a magic wand to fix the special teams issues should deliver it to the team’s football facility. Sarkisian blamed the two major miscues on human error. “I don’t know if there’s, like, fix special teams,” Sarkisian said. “We didn’t set the edge on a punt return and we didn’t field the ball on an onside kick. It wasn’t like they had a free runner and they just got the ball, but we dropped it twice and they got it. That’s human error.” The fake punt came at a critical moment of the second quarter when Texas was up 24-3 and had seemingly forced a three and out by the Ole Miss offense with four minutes remaining and a chance to create more separation before getting the ball to start the second half. Instead, the Rebels were able to keep the ball when the team’s Australian punter started to attempt a rugby punt and saw open turf. “The fake punt really wasn’t even a fake punt. Their guy they called a rugby punt, we didn’t set the edge, and so he just kept running. It really wasn’t a fake — it’s always an option that they have on the play,” Sarkisian said. Oscar Bird ran for 17 yards on the play to keep the Texas defense on the field. FAKE PUNT FAKE PUNT BY OLE MISS!!! THE LONGEST RUSH OF THE NIGHT COMES FROM THE PUNTER pic.twitter.com/3sVqbc2Hvh — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 After the game, sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson took responsibility for failing to set the edge. Normally, his responsibility is to chip the player on the end of the line of scrimmage, which he did, but Banks later told Jackson that he was trying to alert the roll on the rugby punt. In the moment, Jackson couldn’t hear his coach on the sideline. “That’s on me,” Jackson said. Sarkisian was less sure about what happened in the chaos of the onside kick, the second executed success
item.content:encoded: BANGKOK, THAILAND - AUGUST 02: A protester dressed in a Harry Potter themed outfit and wielding a wand campaigns for the freedom of Arnon Nampa during a Harry Potter themed protest at Democracy Monument on August 02, 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand. Pro-democracy activists gather at Democracy Monument during a Harry Potter themed protest called "Letter from Azkaban", calling for constitutional reform and expressing solidarity with political prisoners, most notably Arnon Nampa, a human rights lawyer who is still currently detained after receiving his first prison sentence in a lèse-majesté case. This demonstration marked six years since the original Harry Potter-themed protests that became a symbol of Thailand's youth-led democracy movement. (Photo by Mailee Osten-Tan/Getty Images) | Getty Images AUSTIN — Steve Sarkisian doesn’t have a magic wand to fix the special teams issues that consistently plague his Texas Longhorns. Neither does special teams coordinator Jeff Banks, clearly. After No. 19 Texas beat No. 7 Ole Miss 34-27 in Austin on Saturday despite multiple special teams mishaps, once again, including a successful fake punt and successful onside kick by the Rebels, anyone in possession of a magic wand to fix the special teams issues should deliver it to the team’s football facility. Sarkisian blamed the two major miscues on human error. “I don’t know if there’s, like, fix special teams,” Sarkisian said. “We didn’t set the edge on a punt return and we didn’t field the ball on an onside kick. It wasn’t like they had a free runner and they just got the ball, but we dropped it twice and they got it. That’s human error.” The fake punt came at a critical moment of the second quarter when Texas was up 24-3 and had seemingly forced a three and out by the Ole Miss offense with four minutes remaining and a chance to create more separation before getting the ball to start the second half. Instead, the Rebels were able to keep the ball when the team’s Australian punter started to attempt a rugby punt and saw open turf. “The fake punt really wasn’t even a fake punt. Their guy they called a rugby punt, we didn’t set the edge, and so he just kept running. It really wasn’t a fake — it’s always an option that they have on the play,” Sarkisian said. Oscar Bird ran for 17 yards on the play to keep the Texas defense on the field. FAKE PUNT FAKE PUNT BY OLE MISS!!! THE LONGEST RUSH OF THE NIGHT COMES FROM THE PUNTER pic.twitter.com/3sVqbc2Hvh — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 After the game, sophomore defensive end Lance Jackson took responsibility for failing to set the edge. Normally, his responsibility is to chip the player on the end of the line of scrimmage, which he did, but Banks later told Jackson that he was trying to alert the roll on the rugby punt. In the moment, Jackson couldn’t hear his coach on the sideline. “That’s on me,” Jackson said. Sarkisian was less sure about what happened in the chaos of the onside kick, the second executed successfully against Texas this season, although Tennessee’s effort was ultimately ruled illegal by the conference , for all the good that did after the fact. “We’re there, we just didn’t make the play,” Sarkisian said. “I didn’t see it. I mean, I saw it, but I don’t know exactly what happened with Emmett [Mosley V] and then Graceson [Littleton] and we don’t make the play.” After junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo failed to recover the onside kick against the Volunteers, Banks inserted freshman wide receiver Jermaine Bishop on the hands team instead. Once Ole Miss lined up for the onside kick, Texas took a timeout and flipped its alignment, getting Mosley on the side the Rebels sent the onside kick. But the ball took a big bounce just before it got to Mosley, the normally sure-handed Littleton couldn’t secure it, and Ole Miss came away with it. OLE MISS RECOVERS THE ONSIDE KICK FROM TEXAS OMG 🤯 pic.twitter.com/093ft8L0w9 — ESPN (@espn) October 25, 2026 In both situations, the Texas defense was able to keep Ole Miss from scoring when senior linebacker Rasheem Biles intercepted a pass on the goal line to effectively end the first half and senior safety Jelani McDonald intercepted the Hail Mary attempt by the Rebels to end the game. The Longhorns also committed two penalties on special teams, both by freshman linebacker Kosi Okpala. On the opening kickoff of the second half, Okpala committed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on the touchback, forcing Texas to start its drive on the 12-yard line, contributing to the sack-fumble that resulted in Ole Miss scoring its first touchdown. After the Horns regained the lead on Arch Manning’s one-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter, Okpala was called for another penalty for a late hit out of bounds on a 23-yard kickoff return by the Rebels, allowing Ole Miss to start its drive near midfield. The drive ended with one of the highlights for Texas on special teams — a blocked 58-yard field goal by junior defensive tackle Alex January. TEXAS BLOCKS THE FIELD GOAL THE LONGHORNS DEFENDING THEIR LEAD WELL pic.twitter.com/A8mWyvPY0W — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 Before the play, January told fifth-year defensive tackle Hero Kanu he was going to “get skinny” through the Ole Miss protection. “Okay, I believe you, I trust you,” Kanu replied, helping his fellow defensive lineman and hearing the sound of hand on ball in return. Texas took advantage, driving for a field goal that pushed the margin back to 10 points. Sarkisian pointed to several other positives on special teams, including senior Ryan Niblett returning three punts for 25 yards, senior kicker Gianni Spetic striking the ball better on kickoffs, limiting Ole Miss to the one late return after too many short kicks against Florida resulted in five returns for 105 yards, and senior punter Mac Chiumento turning in his best game of the season by averaging 48.4 yards per punt. Now, if only the Longhorns had that magic wand…

item.title: Cardinals fans take ‘Bidwill Out’ campaign to new heights as owner reportedly fumes
item.description: Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images Arizona Cardinals fans have taken their campaign against Michael Bidwill off social media and onto the roadside. The owner is reportedly furious about it. Two digital billboards now call on Bidwill to sell the team, paid for with more than $8,100 raised by Nathan Kropp, better known on X as @MrAzSports. Chuck Harris of Cardswire reported Bidwill is “incredibly upset” over the #BidwillOut campaign, and told fans to keep the pressure on. Arizona Cardinals fans fund billboards calling on Michael Bidwill to sell The messages are blunt. One reads: “Michael. Please sell the team #BIDWILLOUT Signed, The Fans.” Another says: “SELL THE TEAM, Funded by Cardinals Fans, #BIDWILLOUT.” One sits on westbound Loop 202 shortly before State Route 87, the other off Loop 303 in Surprise. Kropp was moved to act by the Lions game in Week 5, when he felt more away fans were in State Farm Stadium than home ones. “And then I went on X, and people were just completely outraged,” he told FOX. That defeat was Arizona’s ninth straight at home, the longest such run in franchise history. The Cardinals sit 2-4. The frustration runs deeper than one season. The Bidwill family have owned the club since 1932, and Michael took over after his father Bill died in 2019. Arizona have posted one winning season since. There is also the Fitzgerald row. Longtime beat writer Howard Balzer was barred from Larry Fitzgerald’s press conference before his Ring of Honor celebration. “Yeah it’s not right and a really bad look,” one fan wrote . Another added : “What a disgrace of an owner. We all wish we had better!!” A third simply posted : “Another reason that #BidwillOut should happen!” Arizona host Denver next, when Fitzgerald’s No. 11 is retired at halftime. Bidwill has not spoken to reporters since the groundbreaking of the team’s future facilities earlier this year. item.title: Aprilia unsure whether Australian GP cancellation good or bad for the team
item.description: Motorsport photo Aprilia Racing CEO Massimo Rivola says he doesn't know whether the cancellation of Sunday's Australian Grand Prix was good or bad for his team, given Jorge Martín's absence through injury. The marque's lead rider Martin broke his arm on Saturday while fighting for the sprint win, losing the championship lead to Marc Marquez. From his perspective, the cancellation is seen as a small relief and a slight opportunity to remain in the title fight, as not racing prevents his Ducati rival from extending his 10-point lead in the standings. However, Rivola is unsure if the answer is so clear cut for the team as a whole, with Marco Bezzecchi sitting third in the standings and trailing Marquez by 50 points. “I don’t know. I’m sure Marco is a little annoyed because he saw an opportunity,” Rivola explained during a meeting with the media on Sunday at Phillip Island, after the race was cancelled. “But I think Jorge is happy. “I feel sorry for the people who have been here all day, since very early in the morning. And the last dance, let’s say, the last race at Phillip Island deserved a better ending. But that’s how things are.” The organisers cancelled the race because they could not guarantee that the medical helicopter would be able to fly to evacuate any rider injured during the race, or land in Melbourne, where the nearest major referral hospital is located. “Personally, I hadn’t thought about the helicopter issue,” Rivola admitted. “But that was the main problem,” he acknowledged. Massimo Rivola, CEO, Aprilia Racing Massimo Rivola, CEO, Aprilia Racing Rivola spoke to the media immediately after the riders completed two demo laps behind the safety car in front of the thousands of fans who filled the circuit for the last time. “I haven’t spoken to Marco yet after the riders stopped, to find out what the track is like. Judging by what we saw, the track conditions didn’t look very good, considering the average speeds they usually reach here,” he explained, acknowledging that track conditions were not ideal for racing either. “It’s a shame, in a way, because we are here to race, obviously. In fact, the Phillip Island race is one of the most iconic, and we all love coming here. But that’s how things are. I don’t know whether it’s good or not,” he insisted. “I’m here to race” Given Rivola’s ambiguous answer, he was asked again about the issue and for his opinion on whether he was disappointed for Bezzecchi or relieved for Martin. “I don’t know. I’m here to race. So when I come to Phillip Island, I don’t look at the race from a personal perspective. I brought my family because I told them they had to see the last race at Phillip Island. It’s unique. So they spent two or four days travelling back and forth around the world for nothing, but that’s how things are,” he explained. “In the end, if we look at Jorge, it’s clear that it’s better if we don’t race, not even in Sepang, until the final two races, perhaps. But that’s not what we’re thinking ab
item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Aprilia Racing CEO Massimo Rivola says he doesn't know whether the cancellation of Sunday's Australian Grand Prix was good or bad for his team, given Jorge Martín's absence through injury. The marque's lead rider Martin broke his arm on Saturday while fighting for the sprint win, losing the championship lead to Marc Marquez. From his perspective, the cancellation is seen as a small relief and a slight opportunity to remain in the title fight, as not racing prevents his Ducati rival from extending his 10-point lead in the standings. However, Rivola is unsure if the answer is so clear cut for the team as a whole, with Marco Bezzecchi sitting third in the standings and trailing Marquez by 50 points. “I don’t know. I’m sure Marco is a little annoyed because he saw an opportunity,” Rivola explained during a meeting with the media on Sunday at Phillip Island, after the race was cancelled. “But I think Jorge is happy. “I feel sorry for the people who have been here all day, since very early in the morning. And the last dance, let’s say, the last race at Phillip Island deserved a better ending. But that’s how things are.” The organisers cancelled the race because they could not guarantee that the medical helicopter would be able to fly to evacuate any rider injured during the race, or land in Melbourne, where the nearest major referral hospital is located. “Personally, I hadn’t thought about the helicopter issue,” Rivola admitted. “But that was the main problem,” he acknowledged. Massimo Rivola, CEO, Aprilia Racing Massimo Rivola, CEO, Aprilia Racing Rivola spoke to the media immediately after the riders completed two demo laps behind the safety car in front of the thousands of fans who filled the circuit for the last time. “I haven’t spoken to Marco yet after the riders stopped, to find out what the track is like. Judging by what we saw, the track conditions didn’t look very good, considering the average speeds they usually reach here,” he explained, acknowledging that track conditions were not ideal for racing either. “It’s a shame, in a way, because we are here to race, obviously. In fact, the Phillip Island race is one of the most iconic, and we all love coming here. But that’s how things are. I don’t know whether it’s good or not,” he insisted. “I’m here to race” Given Rivola’s ambiguous answer, he was asked again about the issue and for his opinion on whether he was disappointed for Bezzecchi or relieved for Martin. “I don’t know. I’m here to race. So when I come to Phillip Island, I don’t look at the race from a personal perspective. I brought my family because I told them they had to see the last race at Phillip Island. It’s unique. So they spent two or four days travelling back and forth around the world for nothing, but that’s how things are,” he explained. “In the end, if we look at Jorge, it’s clear that it’s better if we don’t race, not even in Sepang, until the final two races, perhaps. But that’s not what we’re thinking about; what matters is what we have to do now. That’s the main task.” It had been known for weeks that heavy rain was forecast for Phillip Island on Sunday, but the race was not moved to Saturday, as it was in 2023. “In fact, Saturday afternoon was also supposed to be quite bad after the Sprint. Today was supposed to be cold and rainy, but not as bad as the previous night. “Perhaps now, talking about whether we could have raced on Saturday, maybe, but it’s too early to say. It’s a shame that we couldn’t race for all these people, but it’s something we really cannot control.” Jorge Martín and Marc Marquez Jorge Martín and Marc Marquez “Very difficult” for Martin to race at Sepang Martin was injured during Saturday's Australian sprint, breaking the radius in his right arm. The non-displaced fracture could allow the Spaniard to race at Sepang next week. “Very difficult. Very, very difficult. I hope to see Jorge in Sepang, at least with us, and we’ll see,” Rivola said. “I think the story between Aprilia and Jorge has been quite unfortunate. The good thing this time is that he has only broken a bone. It’s nothing serious,” he added. “But I would like our story to end in the best possible way, with him at 100% physically. Yesterday, he put on an incredible show. We saw the real Jorge, and I think he had a chance of winning the race. But we can say that sometimes bad things happen. We haven’t had much luck with him, but we certainly won’t give up until this is over.” Following the cancellation in Australia, there is still one grand prix, Qatar, which could also be cancelled, a scenario that would leave Bezzecchi with little chance of winning the title. “On the one hand, there is a lot more to say; on the other, we simply do what we are told. If we do this job, it’s because we are passionate about it. If the organiser tells us that the conditions are suitable for racing from a safety point of view, we simply do it. “We are not in a position to say: ‘I’m not going.’ So far, there is no reason to do so. Perhaps we’ll wake up tomorrow and the situation will have changed, but not today.” “Right now, we believe there are four races left. I don’t know whether that is good or bad for Jorge, because if he isn’t physically fit, it isn’t good. But it’s not up to us to decide that." In case you missed it: MotoGP's final Australian GP at Phillip Island cancelled due to poor weather Jorge Martin planning MotoGP return at Malaysian GP To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Dimarco Contract Talks: Inter and Wing-Back Still Apart on Wages
item.description: Dimarco Contract Talks: Inter and Wing-Back Still Apart on Wages Federico Dimarco and Inter are still some way from agreeing a new contract, with the wing-back’s salary the main sticking point as he also tries to win back his place in the Italy side. According to a report in Tuttosport , the 28-year-old currently earns around €4 million a year. His representatives are said to be asking for €6 million per season, while Inter would be prepared to go to €5 million with bonuses on top. On those numbers the two sides are not miles apart, but nothing has been signed and a middle ground still has to be found. Contract runs to 2027, with a club option Dimarco’s present deal expires on 30 June 2027. The Turin paper adds that Inter intend to use a clause in the contract to push that date back by twelve months to 30 June 2028, which removes any immediate pressure and gives the club time to negotiate. The longer term plan goes further. Earlier this month La Gazzetta dello Sport reported, as relayed by FCInterNews , that talks with the player’s entourage had already opened over an extension running until 2030. Inter have not commented publicly on either report. It is easy to see why the player feels he has earned a rise. Last season he was named the Best Overall player of Serie A 2025/26 , the first defender to win the award, after setting a new league record of 18 assists in a single campaign. Knee problem and Carlos Augusto’s rise The autumn has been far less straightforward. Dimarco hurt his knee in the 3-2 comeback win over Napoli at San Siro and, by Tuttosport’s account, has not yet rediscovered the sharpness that made him so decisive a year ago. In the meantime Carlos Augusto has made the most of his opportunity on the left. The Brazilian has been one of Chivu’s most reliable performers in recent weeks and settled the Champions League meeting with Shakhtar, as we reported after Carlos Augusto’s winner against the Ukrainians . Competition for the role is now genuine, which only adds weight to the contract talks. Italy place under threat There is a national team angle too. Roberto Mancini has returned Italy to a back four, a system that does not suit Dimarco as naturally as his wing-back role at Inter. While he was injured, Arsenal’s Riccardo Calafiori took over at left-back for the Azzurri, a position he already fills in the Premier League. Dimarco has already had one camp cut short this season, when he left the squad after medical checks at Coverciano, as covered in our report on his withdrawal from the Italy squad . Tuttosport notes that Mancini is expected at San Siro to watch Inter in person, so the coming weeks matter for both club and country. What happens next For now, there is no deadline forcing a decision. With the 2028 option available, Inter can keep talking without the risk of losing a key player cheaply, and Dimarco can use the rest of the autumn to show he is back to his best. Whether the gap of roughly €1 million a year is closed quickly

item.title: Jaume Camacho: An introduction to Carrington’s newest breakout star who plundered 4 goals against Liverpool
item.description: Jaume Camacho: An introduction to Carrington’s newest breakout star who plundered 4 goals against Liverpool Manchester United have a habit of developing exciting young players in their youth system. Fans are still reeling from JJ Gabriel’s desire to leave the club after it was announced last month. Nonetheless, players like Noah Ajayi and Kai Rooney are exciting the fanbase. It was the turn of another player yesterday, however. Jaume Camacho plundered four goals against Liverpool under-18s yesterday. Of course, it would be easy just to focus on the quantity of goals, but it was also the quality of the strikes that got fans salivating. The first, in particular, was a sweet dipping strike that dropped into the corner of the goal. It begs the question: who is this ruthless striker United fans will hope can blossom into a first team player in the future? Background The youngster was born in Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. His family then moved to the United Arab Emirates for work when he was a youngster, and he grew up there from the age of just four years old. His first contact with football was with the City Football Group in Abu Dhabi, but the Coronavirus pandemic forced his family to make a decision, and they decided to go to Manchester. Camacho had trials with both City and United as an 11-year-old, and it was the red half of the city who decided to give him a deal. As a result, the youngster has the option of representing Spain, the UAE and England in the future should the 17-year-old have the opportunity to play international football. Style of play The midfielder has been electric this season so far, scoring four goals and providing four assists in all competitions this season for United’s under-18s. He has been described as a “versatile player with the ability to play either in midfield or at full-back.” What’s more, he is “tall and athletic, he covers ground well across the pitch with the ability to dominate games. Camacho is an intelligent player, possessing the composure and technical ability to be a well-rounded midfielder.” Camacho’s growing reputation was reflected in The Guardian choosing him as one of the top 20 best young talents at Premier League clubs for 2026, alongside the likes of Max Dowman. Reflections Like any young player, it will be vital not to pile expectations on the youngster and to let him develop alongside many other talented starlets at the club. Nonetheless, fans can dream of finally taking advantage of the trend of elegant Spanish midfielders, even if his path was slightly off the beaten track compared to the likes of Xavi, Iniesta and Pedri.

Camacho is an intelligent player, possessing the composure and technical ability to be a well-rounded midfielder.” Camacho’s growing reputation was reflected in The Guardian choosing him as one of the top 20 best young talents at Premier League clubs for 2026, alongside the likes of Max Dowman. Reflections Like any young player, it will be vital not to pile expectations on the youngster and to let him develop alongside many other talented starlets at the club. Nonetheless, fans can dream of finally taking advantage of the trend of elegant Spanish midfielders, even if his path was slightly off the beaten track compared to the likes of Xavi, Iniesta and Pedri.

Newcastle United’s new head coach arrived with a CV that deserved a warm welcome. Back-to-back Austrian league titles with Red Bull Salzburg. Consecutive AFC Champions League Elite crowns with Al-Ahli. He is young, ambitious and keen on attacking football, so it is easy to see why he looked like a natural successor to Eddie Howe. When the club appointed him, sporting director Ross Wilson described a leadership style and football philosophy “strongly aligned” with Newcastle’s vision. I beg to differ. A career built on financial muscle? FC Liefering, 2021. His first senior head-coaching job came at Liefering, Red Bull Salzburg’s feeder club in Austria’s second division. Its revenue was 7.8 times the league average and its wage bill was 4.3 times that of its peers. He had access to facilities, players and finances that the other clubs in the league could only dream of. Red Bull Salzburg, 2021–23. The gap grew wider. Revenue was 8.7 times the Austrian Bundesliga average, the wage bill was 6.2 times higher than those of domestic rivals, and the club’s income made up 44 per cent of the league’s total. Matthias Jaissle won two league titles and took Salzburg into the Champions League knockout stages, at a club already established as the dominant force in Austrian football. Al-Ahli. Next came Al-Ahli, one of four clubs majority owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. A squad featuring Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino and Ivan Toney cost around €380 million in transfers across his three seasons. Players of that calibre do not come to clubs in Saudi Arabia without very big wages behind them. Al-Ahli are big spenders, one of the four big spenders in the country. Al-Hilal, Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli all sit under the PIF umbrella, and their resources dwarf everyone else’s in the division. That makes it a four-club mini league within the league, and the fairest place to judge Jaissle, because the money on each side is broadly similar. Over three seasons, he failed to finish higher than third in a four-team mini league. In one season he finished fifth. The Asian triumphs, in context. Two Asian titles in a row is a big achievement.
