Newcastle United’s new head coach arrived with a CV that deserved a warm welcome. Back-to-back Austrian league titles with Red Bull Salzburg. Consecutive AFC Champions League Elite crowns with Al-Ahli. He is young, ambitious and keen on attacking football, so it is easy to see why he looked like a natural successor to Eddie Howe. When the club appointed him, sporting director Ross Wilson described a leadership style and football philosophy “strongly aligned” with Newcastle’s vision. I beg to differ. A career built on financial muscle? FC Liefering, 2021. His first senior head-coaching job came at Liefering, Red Bull Salzburg’s feeder club in Austria’s second division. Its revenue was 7.8 times the league average and its wage bill was 4.3 times that of its peers. He had access to facilities, players and finances that the other clubs in the league could only dream of. Red Bull Salzburg, 2021–23. The gap grew wider. Revenue was 8.7 times the Austrian Bundesliga average, the wage bill was 6.2 times higher than those of domestic rivals, and the club’s income made up 44 per cent of the league’s total. Matthias Jaissle won two league titles and took Salzburg into the Champions League knockout stages, at a club already established as the dominant force in Austrian football. Al-Ahli. Next came Al-Ahli, one of four clubs majority owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. A squad featuring Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino and Ivan Toney cost around €380 million in transfers across his three seasons. Players of that calibre do not come to clubs in Saudi Arabia without very big wages behind them. Al-Ahli are big spenders, one of the four big spenders in the country. Al-Hilal, Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli all sit under the PIF umbrella, and their resources dwarf everyone else’s in the division. That makes it a four-club mini league within the league, and the fairest place to judge Jaissle, because the money on each side is broadly similar. Over three seasons, he failed to finish higher than third in a four-team mini league. In one season he finished fifth. The Asian triumphs, in context. Two Asian titles in a row is a big achievement. It takes preparation, tactical flexibility and a cool head under pressure. But there is huge disparity in this competition. Al-Ahli’s second title was a hard-fought win: Jaissle’s side beat Machida Zelvia 1-0 after extra time in April 2026, seeing out the closing stages with ten men. In the 2025 final, Al-Ahli beat Kawasaki Frontale. They outspent the Japanese club on transfers by 12.9 to 1 over the season. A year later, they defended their title against Machida Zelvia, who spent 16.1 times less on transfers. In terms of spending, the equivalent is Real Madrid meeting Preston North End in a final. This summer Real Madrid spent about 14 times as much as Preston. The trophies show Matthias Jaissle can manage an expensively assembled side. They leave open whether he can outperform clubs with greater financial power. Why it matters Newcastle’s revenue of €398.4 million makes them eighth in the Premier League and 17th in Europe, according to the most recent Deloitte report (Published in January 2026 covering the 2024/25 season accounts for all clubs). They want to force their way into the top four or five against clubs with enormous resources and Jaissle has never worked in a league as deep. Rúben Amorim arrived at Manchester United with a big reputation and a 71% win percentage at Sporting CP across all competitions. His Premier League record when he left was only 32%. He left with his reputation in tatters and his tail between his legs but with a big fat pay cheque to boot. Jaissle’s CV has the same shape: big advantages over domestic rivals, then a move into a league where the gap is far smaller. We should expect the same. The golden rule is having a manager who can punch above his weight. Newcastle United has money but not enough to compete against those financially above us. The manager needs to outperform the budget. He must make the money stretch further. He needs to do more with less. That is the job at Newcastle. That’s what Eddie Howe did. That’s what Unai Emery is doing. And that’s what Matthias Jaissle has never done. And that’s what the recruitment team missed. The Newcastle United recruitment team’s mistake was to look at a record of wins and not ask what stood behind them. All of it sits in public data, and in an era when every top club has analysts and data at its fingertips, there is no excuse for missing it. The decision Either Matthias Jaissle learns to win without the biggest budget (something he failed to do in three years in Saudi), or he is sacked. On the data alone, Newcastle United have the wrong man. It is exactly what Manchester United did with Rúben Amorim . Many are comparing him with Amorim, with his tactical inflexibility. That is not the issue. The issue is he has never won anything when he has not got more money than anyone else. By all means, give him a run of games. But have no doubt, he is the wrong man, and he never should have been given the opportunity. History has shown that he does not have the ability to over perform. We cannot let our club fall into the Championship based upon a recruitment error. A mistake has been made, and we need to move on quickly. Source

item.title: Whole city on his back: Bundesliga fanatic desperately needs a win
item.description: Whole city on his back: Bundesliga fanatic desperately needs a win “I have the Sandro Wagner gene. I want to win every game. I’m a bit of a freak that way,” Sandro Wagner stressed in the summer of 2021 when he took over as Unterhaching coach. Five years later, the self-proclaimed freak is in charge of Hannover 96 and has so far been desperately trying to inject his team with the “Sandro Wagner gene.” But today, more than ever, the coach had better hope his injection has worked. Because he could have the entire city breathing down his neck. That might sound a little exaggerated at first. But only at first. Because the Reds’ match today at 1:30 p.m. is no ordinary fixture for Sandro Wagner. Hannover 96 visit Eintracht Braunschweig for one of Germany’s biggest derbies. Just how much can these clashes mean to an entire city? Let’s ask Said El Mala. All of Cologne recently celebrated their superstar after he fired FC to a 2–1 derby win over Gladbach. “Every Bundesliga goal is special, but scoring in a derby is something else,” the 20-year-old enthused to 'Sky' afterwards. At Schalke, children will probably still know Naldo’s name in 20 years, after his header completed the Royal Blues’ comeback from 4–0 down to draw 4–4 in 2017. But while heroes are celebrated on one side, the mood on the other can turn sour incredibly quickly. Hannover’s ultras provided the perfect example in the spring of 2023. After Hannover lost 1–0 at Braunschweig, they vented their anger outside their own stadium. Hours after the game, they rioted outside the former Niedersachsenstadion and ultimately had to be pushed back by police using water cannons. At the time, 96 had gone nine games without a win. Things are not looking much better under Wagner right now. Little has gone right for the coach since he took over a few weeks ago. A crushing 3–0 opening defeat to Magdeburg was followed by a disappointing 1–1 draw against St. Pauli on his home debut. Clearly nowhere near good enough for a club with promotion ambitions. 96 currently sit 14th in the table. Another defeat could, in the worst case, leave them as many as ten points off the promotion places. They could also slip into the relegation play-off spot. item.title: The Army Officer playing for Wales at a World Cup
item.description: Jade Mullen is the captain of the Army rugby union team [WALES RUGBY LEAGUE] Jade Mullen's journey to the Women's Rugby League World Cup has been an unconventional one. A last-minute code switch within the sport allowed her to earn a place in Wales' squad for the showpiece tournament in Australia. Mullen has plenty of rugby union experience having captained the Army's team at high-profile venues like Twickenham. But she had never played rugby league before January this year after Wales captain Bethan Dainton, who is also enlisted in the British Army, encouraged her to try the 13-a-side game. She started training with London Broncos and the rest, as they say, is history. "Me and Bethan have been close friends for a few years. She's played rugby league much longer than me and she always said that I'd enjoy it, so I thought I'd give it a go," Mullen explained. "I joined London Broncos at the start of the season so was training with them from January onwards ready for the season to kick off in March. I fell in love with the sport so I'm really enjoying it. "For a while I was training twice a week at London Broncos and then also doing rugby union training at the same time. That was tiring." Mullen's venture into rugby league has paid off. Not only has she represented Wales in both games so far at the World Cup in Australia, she also was part of the London Broncos squad that won the National Championship to earn promotion to the Super League. During that period she also had to play for the Army, and is grateful to the Broncos for their support. "Luckily London Broncos were really understanding. They knew that the Army is my full-time job and that I was captain of the team, so they were really supportive of me," Mullen said. "They gave me two or three weeks off and then I went straight back to the Broncos and we finished on a high with the season we had. "We grew as a team during the season. I enjoyed the physicality and I just love defending. "I probably would say rugby league is a bit more physical. My union friends will probably hate that I've said that." Mullen helped London Broncos win promotion to the Women's Super League [WALES RUGBY LEAGUE] Mullen left home at the age of 17 to join the British Army, and it was there she was introduced to rugby union. "I picked up the sport when I joined the Army," Mullen recalled. "I wanted to improve my skill set and looked into club rugby. I started out for Pencoed back in Wales and then went to Worcester Valkyries. "I then got picked by Harlequins in 2018 and stayed with them until last year." The 34-year-old, originally from Caerphilly, combines rugby with her military duties as a warrant officer currently attached to 1st Battalion, the Coldstream Guards in Windsor. As captain of the Army team she led them to victory over the Navy at Twickenham in 2023. "It was amazing. Being Welsh as well going to Twickenham and winning there is massive. "To win the inter-services, which is a massive competition, is some achievement. So to lift the trophy there was pretty surreal." Wales lost 76-0 against Samoa in their second group game [Getty Images] Wales are competing in the World Cup for the first time in their history. They are in a challenging group and have lost heavily against England and Samoa in their opening two games. They face another daunting test in their final group match against hosts Australia who are the current world champions. It was always going to be a tough ask for Wales to finish in the top two to qualify for the semi-finals, but competing on the biggest stage has meant the players have received plenty of support from back home. "My family have supported me my whole career obviously because I left home at the age of 17. So, they've always supported me from a distance," said Mullen. "The Army rugby team are currently in Canada and they've sent me their best wishes. "It's the first Army rugby union fixture I've missed for the last couple of seasons. The fact they've messaged and cheered me on from Canada is pretty special too."

The Valkyries attempted more than double the number of shots Dream did (40 vs. 19), and led 42-26. Now, as the series heads to Chase Center tied 2-2, Golden State has a chance to carry the momentum into Game 5. item.title: AC Milan plotting €50m summer move for Man United defender Leny Yoro
item.description: AC Milan plotting €50m summer move for Man United defender Leny Yoro AC Milan are considering a summer move for Manchester United defender Leny Yoro, according to Calciomercato . The Italian giants see the Frenchman as a potential solution to their defensive problems ahead of next season. Milan have identified the 20-year-old as a key target, and a deal is expected to cost between €40 million and €50 million. The Rossoneri also hope Yoro’s representative, Jorge Mendes, who represents Goncalo Ramos and manager Ruben Amorim, can help facilitate negotiations with Man United. Milan want to add more depth to their defensive options. Besides their starting back three of Strahinja Pavlovic, Koni de Winter, and Mario Gila, they are short. Gabbia is injured, and Amorim clearly isn’t a fan of Fikayo Tomori, whom he has used sparingly. Several other defenders are also on Milan’s radar, including Nottingham Forest’s Ousmane Diomande and Bayern Munich’s Kim Min-jae, but they are January options. Diomande remains high on their shortlist, while Kim is another attractive option. However, the South Korean’s salary demands could complicate any deal, and Bayern Munich are also reluctant to sanction an early January departure. Milan have also explored signing Daniele Ghilardi from Roma, while Mendes is trying to facilitate a loan move for Lecce defender Thiago Gabriel. Yoro’s situation at Old Trafford could prove crucial to Milan’s pursuit. There is currently no indication that Man United are prepared to part ways with the young defender, but they are set for a defensive overhaul. The Frenchman arrived from Lille in 2024 after establishing himself as one of Europe’s most promising defensive prospects. United beat competition from several leading clubs, including Paris Saint-Germain, to secure his signature. However, he has struggled to stand out for the Red Devils because of their structural issues on and off the field. Still, he remains a talented prospect. His physical profile is perfect, but he may need a more stable environment to shine. Milan will believe they can offer that, but their situation in Italy may be just as turbulent and worrying as Man United’s.

item.title: Wow, the English Roberto Firmino belongs to Liverpool, he's incredible
item.description: Wow, the English Roberto Firmino belongs to Liverpool, he's incredible Liverpool have an incredibly exciting young player who plays just like Roberto Firmino. The Reds have a clear strategy. In order to get back to the pinnacle of European football, to experience the glory days under Jurgen Klopp, Liverpool are now bringing in the best young players from all across the globe. At senior level we've seen this translate to the signings of Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Jeremy Jacquet. However, at youth level there has been an even more aggressive recruitment plan. Liverpool have brought in Will Wright, Armin Pecsi, Mor Talla Ndiaye, Ifeanyi Ndukwe, Samuel Martinez, Djylian N'Guessan and Lucca Brughmans. More young players are also being targeted by Liverpool with Julian Ward keen to recruit the best in the world. Julian Ward's plans for Liverpool's next signings Liverpool have recently invited two trialists from The Gambia. Sheriff Bah and Musa Jatta are both believed to have impressed the Reds' coaching staff. Ward's also eyeing Daniel Banjaqui, who Pedro Marques spotted at the U17 World Cup and who is seen as the perfect right-back for the club. There's also strong interest in Gilberto Mora. Liverpool are one of the frontrunners in the race to sign the Mexican sensation. However, no final agreement has been reached. There's a strong chance Mora could end-up at Anfield though. Justin Ellis is another player on the club's radar. As is David Otorbi. The two teenagers have both caught the eye over the course of the last year. Ellis is a stand-out talent in the MLS, meanwhile Otorbi has caught the eye for Valencia. Meet Liverpool's new Firmino - Kobi Akerele There are also some exciting talents within Liverpool's own academy. There's high hopes for Joshua Abe and Luca Eden as well as Patrik Farkas. AJ Yeguo has recently started to catch the eye as well. But there's another exciting young player. Kobi Akerele has six goals and seven assists for Liverpool at U16 and U17 level this season and he made history with England's youth national team as well. The young striker earned a call-up for the Three Lions competing at the U15 World Cup. It's the first time the tournament is taking place and Akerele scored England's first goal at the tournament netting during a 4-0 victory for his nation. A small and creative forward. Akerele plays like Roberto Firmino being both a facilitator and a goal-scorer. He is a typical false nine with great technical qualities and someone who could easily replicate the Reds' former Brazilian in the future.

item.title: Devils GM Turns Back on His Word With Blockbuster Trade
item.description: SUNRISE, FLORIDA - JUNE 24: Sunny Mehta and Bryan McCabe of the Florida Panthers celebrate their Stanley Cup victory in Game Seven of the 2024 NHL Stanley Cup Final at Amerant Bank Arena on June 24, 2024 in Sunrise, Florida. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty Sunny Mehta hasn’t been in charge of the New Jersey Devils for very long, as he was named the team’s new general manager on April 16, but he’s already going back on his word. When the Devils’ general manager spoke to NHL.com’s Mike Monreale back in September, just over a month ago, “There are objective measures such as save percentage and wins, but this is also about allocating resources in a salary-cap league. Money spent in goal cannot be spent somewhere else,” Mehta told Monreale on September 20. “Because there is randomness at the position, I’m reluctant to invest significant assets there instead of in areas where the results may be more predictable.” Now, not only did Mehta go back on his prior statement by swinging a massive trade to bring Olympic gold medalist Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey, he also did it in the most unpredictable way possible by bringing in a 33-year-old signed through 2031. A Down Season Although Hellebuyck was phenomenal for Team USA at the 2026 Winter Olympic Games, helping them earn a gold medal over their Canadian counterparts, he struggled quite a bit compared to his normal standard during the NHL’s regular season. In 57 games, he recorded a .895 save percentage, down from a .925 the season before. He also allowed nearly an additional goal per game, as his goals against average jumped from 2.01 in the 2024-25 season to 2.86 last season. Of course, quite a bit of his performance can be tied to the Winnipeg Jets underperforming as a whole, but given the fact that he forced his way out of the market after failing to contribute to the team’s success last season is a bit of a red flag. Hellbuyck Getting Helle-bucks A key thing that Mehta mentioned in his interview with Monreale was the fact that he didn’t want to spend money on goaltending because of the randomness and high cost of the position. While that makes sense to an extent, it counteracts how the Florida Panthers found success when he was in their organization. When the Panthers won their Stanley Cups, they were paying Sergei Bobrovsky $10 million per season. Of course, Bobrovsky is exactly the type of goaltender that Mehta mentioned, as his performance is very unpredictable at times, but it seems odd that he’d make a statement counteracting his past success. Hellebuyck’s contract isn’t quite as big as Bobrovsky’s was in Florida, but it’s still fairly sizeable considering goaltender contracts haven’t taken the same jump that we’ve seen in every other position as of late. The highest-paid goaltender in the league is Igor Shesterkin, whose cap hit of roughly $11.5 million, is the only current salary for a goaltender to reach seven figures. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Getty Sunny Mehta hasn’t been in charge of the New Jersey Devils for very long, as he was named the team’s new general manager on April 16, but he’s already going back on his word. Money spent in goal cannot be spent somewhere else,” Mehta told Monreale on September 20. “Because there is randomness at the position, I’m reluctant to invest significant assets there instead of in areas where the results may be more predictable.” Now, not only did Mehta go back on his prior statement by swinging a massive trade to bring Olympic gold medalist Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey, he also did it in the most unpredictable way possible by bringing in a 33-year-old signed through 2031. Of course, quite a bit of his performance can be tied to the Winnipeg Jets underperforming as a whole, but given the fact that he forced his way out of the market after failing to contribute to the team’s success last season is a bit of a red flag. While that makes sense to an extent, it counteracts how the Florida Panthers found success when he was in their organization. When the Panthers won their Stanley Cups, they were paying Sergei Bobrovsky $10 million per season. Of course, Bobrovsky is exactly the type of goaltender that Mehta mentioned, as his performance is very unpredictable at times, but it seems odd that he’d make a statement counteracting his past success. Hellebuyck’s contract isn’t quite as big as Bobrovsky’s was in Florida, but it’s still fairly sizeable considering goaltender contracts haven’t taken the same jump that we’ve seen in every other position as of late. The highest-paid goaltender in the league is Igor Shesterkin, whose cap hit of roughly $11.5 million, is the only current salary for a goaltender to reach seven figures. Hellebuyck is currently the eighth-highest paid goaltender in the NHL and he’s also tied for the oldest player in the top ten with Linus Ullmark who sits just ahead of him in seventh. While it’s always hard to hold an executive in sports to their word, it seems odd that one of Mehta’s first major moves in charge of the New Jersey Devils revolves around him acquiring the type of player he bluntly stated that he didn’t want. Only time will tell if he made the right call to turn back on his word or if changing away from his principle will set the team back. item.title: World Series winners and losers: Amazing Ashby, manager misfires, check-swing drama
item.description: MILWAUKEE – This World Series is set to move on from Dairyland, but not before a chicken-or-the-egg question is settled: Are the Tampa Bay Rays blowing it on the big stage , or are the Milwaukee Brewers forcing them to act like imposters and not the 98-win American League champions? The answer is relatively immaterial, since only one thing matters: The Brewers are up 2-0 in this World Series after a 5-4 Game 2 victory, their second one-run conquest and a most unlikely one given that the club trailed 4-0 after a half-inning. Or maybe it was totally predictable. The Brewers are now 9-1 in this postseason and, stunningly, have won seven of eight games in which they have trailed. Relentless. Demoralizing. Two wins from a World Series championship. Let’s break down the winners and losers of Game 2 from American Family Field as the Series shifts to the Gulf Coast: Winner: Brewers bullpen This is getting ridiculous. The Rays ran a blitz on Brewers starter Logan Henderson, posting a 4-0 lead after a half-inning, catcher Liam Hicks achieving a career highlight with a two-run World Series home run. Predictably, Henderson was out after three innings. Perhaps even more easily anticipated: Milwaukee’s bullpen did not give up a single run in six innings, striking out six and walking one. The Brewers bullpen is now 8-1 with a 1.24 ERA in 50 ⅔ innings this season. Lefty Aaron Ashby recorded the last five outs for the save, running his postseason line to 15 ⅔ innings, zero runs. "I’ll take this quote from Freddie Freeman: They all throw 100," says Rays outfielder Jonny DeLuca. "That usually is pretty tough and they all got pretty good stuff. They’re just good pitchers." Ashby is one out shy of equaling Andrew Miller’s record 16-inning scoreless streak to begin the 2016 postseason. “What he's doing right now is pretty special,” says first baseman Jake Bauers. “There's just such a calm presence on the mound with him right now that I don't remember seeing very often. “And you know, we wouldn't be here without him.” There tend to be diminishing returns with relievers in long postseasons; Miller hit the wall badly in the final three games of that 2016 World Series, and conventional wisdom says opponents fare better when they see a reliever multiple times. Well, Ashby faced the San Diego Padres three times. Same with the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers . And now the Tampa Bay Rays got two looks at him in World Series Games 1 and 2. Ashby has yet to give up a run. The window to sully him is almost closed. Sal Frelick: Winner Say this for Brewers manager Pat Murphy: He can certainly call his shot. Murphy was asked pregame about Frelick and couldn’t stop gushing, dropping comparisons to Joe Montana and Larry Bird. “He’s got the it factor,” says Murphy, leaving the observer to use their own imagination. item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE – This World Series is set to move on from Dairyland, but not before a chicken-or-the-egg question is settled: Are the Tampa Bay Rays blowing it on the big stage , or are the Milwaukee Brewers forcing them to act like imposters and not the 98-win American League champions? The answer is relatively immaterial, since only one thing matters: The Brewers are up 2-0 in this World Series after a 5-4 Game 2 victory, their second one-run conquest and a most unlikely one given that the club trailed 4-0 after a half-inning. Or maybe it was totally predictable. The Brewers are now 9-1 in this postseason and, stunningly, have won seven of eight games in which they have trailed. Relentless. Demoralizing. Two wins from a World Series championship. Let’s break down the winners and losers of Game 2 from American Family Field as the Series shifts to the Gulf Coast: Winner: Brewers bullpen This is getting ridiculous. The Rays ran a blitz on Brewers starter Logan Henderson, posting a 4-0 lead after a half-inning, catcher Liam Hicks achieving a career highlight with a two-run World Series home run. Predictably, Henderson was out after three innings. Perhaps even more easily anticipated: Milwaukee’s bullpen did not give up a single run in six innings, striking out six and walking one. The Brewers bullpen is now 8-1 with a 1.24 ERA in 50 ⅔ innings this season. Lefty Aaron Ashby recorded the last five outs for the save, running his postseason line to 15 ⅔ innings, zero runs. "I’ll take this quote from Freddie Freeman: They all throw 100," says Rays outfielder Jonny DeLuca. "That usually is pretty tough and they all got pretty good stuff. They’re just good pitchers." Ashby is one out shy of equaling Andrew Miller’s record 16-inning scoreless streak to begin the 2016 postseason. “What he's doing right now is pretty special,” says first baseman Jake Bauers. “There's just such a calm presence on the mound with him right now that I don't remember seeing very often. “And you know, we wouldn't be here without him.” There tend to be diminishing returns with relievers in long postseasons; Miller hit the wall badly in the final three games of that 2016 World Series, and conventional wisdom says opponents fare better when they see a reliever multiple times. Well, Ashby faced the San Diego Padres three times. Same with the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers . And now the Tampa Bay Rays got two looks at him in World Series Games 1 and 2. Ashby has yet to give up a run. The window to sully him is almost closed. Sal Frelick: Winner Say this for Brewers manager Pat Murphy: He can certainly call his shot. Murphy was asked pregame about Frelick and couldn’t stop gushing, dropping comparisons to Joe Montana and Larry Bird. “He’s got the it factor,” says Murphy, leaving the observer to use their own imagination. In the sixth inning, Frelick made it crystal clear. His epic nine-pitch at-bat ended in a 408-foot bullet over the wall in right center field, tying the game 4-4 in the sixth inning. It was his first homer this postseason and perhaps will be remembered as the most impactful longball whenever this Brewers run concludes. “Sort of this blackout feeling,” says Frelick of his trip around the bases. And almost lights out for Tampa Bay. Kevin Cash: Loser Tough gig, this postseason managing. And losing a pair of World Series games by one run can leave a winter worth of soul-searching. Not that Cash blatantly pushed the wrong buttons. He just keeps ending up in tight situations and trying to leverage his way out of them. In Game 2, it was ace Drew Rasmussen suddenly becoming an avatar of inefficiency, the Brewers hen-pecking him by fouling off 22 pitches and forcing him from the game in the fourth inning. Top lefty reliever Cam Booser had to be summoned then to douse a bases-loaded situaoitn and pitched a scoreless fifth. But Ian Seymour’s fusillade of fastballs backfired when Frelick took him deep. And lifting Tyler Wells for Kevin Kelly yielded a somewhat predictable result in the seventh inning: Kelly averaged less than a strikeout per inning this season. And Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt, well, he put the ball in play, dropping a 90-mph sinker into right field to drive in Brice Turang with the go-ahead run. “Cooper Pratt did a heck of a job staying on the ball, not trying to do too much, and shoot it the other way,” says Cash. Stolen bases: Winner The Brewers tallied five, the Rays two. Not to say the Go-Go Era is back in baseball; it was mostly pitcher malfeasance/indifference to keeping runners close. Nonetheless, the Brewers’ five steals matched the 2024 Yankees in Game 4; the last time a club stole five bases in a World Series game minus today’s freewheeling pickoff rules was 1992, when Atlanta did it thanks to two swipes from none other than Deion Sanders. The mystery of the check swing: Loser Yeah, that automated check-swing replay thing is probably a foregone conclusion now, given how this game ended with Yandy Díaz’s arms spread wide in protest after crew chief James Hoye rang him up. Cash thought Díaz swung, and Yandy generally agreed, though he did drop a couple “It is what it is,” a phrase that drops like a brick in any language. Still, the call wasn’t nearly as questionable as, say, Wilmer Flores’ NLDS-ending strikeout against Max Scherzer and the Los Angeles Dodgers. Yet in our societal thirst for optimization, we will probably leave those calls up to robots soon enough, too. Tampa Bay ticket brokers: Loser Nothing quite like a team coming home in a 2-0 deficit to goose enthusiasm when the club has struggled to sell all tickets, anyway. Seats were still available on the Rays web site - running $675 apiece for the second level. Suffice to say, the Rays likely won't come near the $2,300 get-in record Milwaukee set for Game 1. But there could be a nice boost in Games 4 and 5 - what with Milwaukeeans wanting to see their team clinch . item.title: UH falters in second half as No. 14 Cougars can't finish in loss to No. 10 Utah
item.description: UH's defense had no answer for Utah quarterback Devon Dampier, either running or passing, as the Cougars lost control during the second half of Saturday's game in Salt Lake City. (Jeffrey D. Allred/AP Photo/Jeffrey D. Allred) SALT LAKE CITY - On a day of chaos in the Big 12, the University of Houston couldn't deliver the final blow early Sunday morning. The No. 14 Cougars blew a 10-point lead as No. 10 Utah's stable of backs and quarterback Devon Dampier pushed them around in a 21-13 loss at Rice-Eccles Stadium. UH threw four incomplete passes to end its final threat, the last a 23-yard throw from Conner Weigman to Koby Young in the back of the end zone. The Utes had extended the lead when Jackson Bennee blitzed untouched and knocked the ball loose from Weigman at the UH 10-yard line. The Utes capitalized on the next play, a touchdown run by Dampier to extend the nation's longest active winning streak to 13. Entering Saturday, the Big 12 was the only conference with three remaining unbeaten teams. They ended the day with one. Cincinnati took down No. 8 Texas Tech . UCF knocked off No. 2 BYU in double overtime. In the nightcap, the Cougars (6-2, 3-2 Big 12) couldn't hold a 10-point lead and had no answer for Dampier, who ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns. He accounted for 354 yards of total offense and all three touchdowns. Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) moved into sole possession of first place in the conference. UH had forced the Utes to punt with about 2 ½ minutes left. On the first play, Weigman took the snap and was hit from the blindside by Bennee, who jarred the ball loose and killed any chance of the Cougars' first top-10 road win since 2009. SALT LAKE CITY, UT - OCTOBER 24: Houston Cougars defensive back Kentrell Webb (8) celebrates after intercepting a pass during a college football game between the Houston Cougars and Utah Utes on October 24, 2026 at Rice Eccles Stadium at Salt Lake City, Utah (Photo by Boyd Ivey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) (Boyd Ivey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Utah and UH entered as two of the Big 12's most explosive offenses, both averaging around 40 points per game. They combined for three points in the first half - a 24-yard field goal by UH's Jonathan Dimas. Makhi Hughes' 2-yard run put the Cougars ahead 10-0, an authoritative 15-play, 75-yard drive opening drive of the second half that took more than eight minutes off the clock. After being held scoreless more than 40 minutes, Utah answered with a quick five-play, 75-yard drive that took less than 2 ½ minutes. Dampier completed a couple short passes and did the rest with his legs with 50 yards, the last 22 on the Utes' only touchdown. Dimas added a career-long 47-yard field goal in the third quarter. Wayshawn Parker's 5-yard touchdown run gave Utah its first lead, 14-13, with about 12 minutes left in the game. Amare Thomas finished with five catches for 133 yards. Weigman, who played with a noticeable limp, was 19-of-34 for 282 yards and no touchdowns. Weigman hooked up on a 41-yard completion to Young to the Utah 23 in the closing minutes. But the Cougars could get no closer. UH once again struggled close to the goal line, coming up empty on fourth-and-1 from the Utah 3 and settling for a field goal after moving inside the 5. UH's defense came up with two momentum-swinging plays, an interception by safety Kentrell Webb in the end zone early in the second quarter and McCutchin's pick deep in UH territory with 7:57 left. UH played most of the game without star tight end Patrick Overmyer, who suffered an upper-body injury on the Cougars' opening drive and did not return. item.title: Weather causes cancellation of MotoGP in Australia
item.description: Reigning champion Marc Marquez has won four times at Phillip Island in the top class [Getty Images] Sunday's MotoGP race in Australia was cancelled because of bad weather at Phillip Island. The race, which would have been the final one at the legendary circuit off the coast of Melbourne, was delayed and then cancelled because of rain and poor visibility. After cancelling the earlier Moto 2 and Moto 3 races, organisers tried to get the MotoGP race on by pushing it back several hours. The track looked dry in some areas as the rain eased off. But, ultimately, a lack of visibility meant that medical helicopters would be unable to fly over the circuit, which led to the decision to cancel the race. Race director Graham Webb said: "The helicopter needs a window of around 60 minutes in both places - Phillip Island and Melbourne - in order for us to start the race. "Just based on safety, we need to make sure that, if we do have any issues, we're covered, we can get a rider quickly to hospital. "Most circuits, we can reach a circuit within 45 minutes, which is our regulation, but here in Phillip Island the hospital is further than 45 minutes by road and therefore we rely on the air ambulance." Reigning champion Marc Marquez leads the standings by 10 points with four races left. The Australian MotoGP is moving to a new street circuit in Adelaide from next season. Other than two years lost to the coronavirus pandemic, Phillip Island has been a ​fixture on ⁠the world championship calendar for 30 years. Australian two-time world champion Casey Stoner celebrated six wins in succession from 2007 to 2012, while compatriot Mick Doohan sealed his fifth and final world title with victory in the 1998 race. item.title: Where to watch Kansas vs. Duke basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for men's exhibition game
item.description: Where to watch Kansas vs. Duke basketball: Channel, live stream, time, TV schedule for men's exhibition game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's only the preseason, but it doesn't get much better than Duke vs. Kansas, and two of the most storied programs in college basketball will get a national stage for Sunday's exhibition game. The Blue Devils are ranked second in the AP Top 25 and look every bit of it through a pair of exhibition games. It was no surprise to see them blow out Belmont by 40 in their preseason opener, but it was something else entirely when they ripped No. 8 Tennessee by nearly the same score, 103-64, on Tuesday. Duke made 12 3-pointers in that one while holding the Vols to 4 of 18 from beyond the arc. Freshman Deron Rippey Jr. (21 points) and Wisconsin transfer John Blackwell (18 points) did most of the long-range damage for the Blue Devils in that one, while four other Duke players also reached double digits. The Jayhawks, on the other hand, will be looking to bounce back after falling at home to No. 11 Louisville on Wednesday. Tre White was the primary bright spot in defeat for KU with 25 points, while Melvin Council Jr. added 20 and highly touted freshman Tyran Stokes had 15 points and a game-high nine rebounds. Plenty of eyes will be on this matchup even if it doesn't count. Here's all you need to know to watch. Where to watch Kansas vs. Duke basketball TV channel: ESPN Live stream: Fubo The Kansas vs. Duke exhibition game will be broadcast nationally on ESPN, with Rich Hollenberg and Sean Farnham on the call, and can be streamed live on Fubo . Fubo offers a free trial for new subscribers, so you can try the service before you buy. Stream ESPN, ABC, CBS, Fox, NBC and 100+ top channels of live TV and sports without cable. (Participating plans only. Taxes and fees may apply.) What time is Kansas vs. Duke today? Date: Sunday, Oct. 25 Time: 1 p.m. ET | 12 p.m. CT Kansas vs. Duke is set to tip off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. The game will be played at Allen Fieldhouse in Lawrence, Kansas. It's Duke's first visit to Lawrence since the 1988 season, when the Blue Devils beat the Jayhawks during the regular season but KU got revenge in the Final Four on the way to a national title. item.title: Farke's assessment of 'handful' Sunderland star and the trap Leeds must avoid
item.description: Farke's assessment of 'handful' Sunderland star and the trap Leeds must avoid Leeds United and Daniel Farke will not fall into a trap laid out for them by the early Premier League table. A tally of 10 points from the opening seven fixtures, with just one defeat, had Leeds in seventh place ahead of the weekend. Sunday's hosts Sunderland have earned just four points in the same period, losing five times. No matter the results elsewhere before the top flight's last game of the weekend, the Black Cats will sit bottom when they kick off against Leeds. Last weekend's game against Manchester United brought the word 'expectation' to the fore around Elland Road and the longer Leeds stay in and around the top half of the table, the more games they will go into with the favourites tag. But regardless of the two sides' contrasting fortunes in the early days of the 2026/27 Premier League season, Farke insists he is all too aware of the challenge Sunderland will pose on Sunday. "I know exactly what to expect because they played with similar processes like they did under Régis Le Bris in the last years," he said. "He brought big success to them with promotion. Also fantastic last season, qualifying for Europe. Of course, second year after promotion is quite often a bit difficult, especially once you have also the additional load from Europe. There were also tight games on Premier League level and it's still early doors, just the seventh game day. I'm pretty sure they won't finish on the position where they are currently in." Farke's expectation is that Sunderland will be well up for the fight on home soil. "I also expect a team who plays also to their plans and to their DNA and also what they've done over the last seasons. Many teams found it very difficult to travel to the Stadium of Light. And we know also how difficult it is be competitive there. We had good away games over the last seasons. And we want to do the same. But we expect also a Sunderland side who will be highly motivated and will be back to their best." Some of Sunderland's difficulties this season can be attributed to injury issues and key absentees. Centre-back Dan Ballard has been missing through a hamstring problem. But as Thomas Muenier and Wilson Isidor progress towards returns, the Black Cats have been bolstered by the news that Brian Brobbey is expected to be available for Sunday's clash. "It seems like important players have also missed out during the last weeks," said Farke. "I'm pretty sure once they come back, they have all chances to shine. But we want to make sure that it's not on Sunday they start to shine again. We want to be successful ourselves. "[The returning Brobbey] is a handful. And he has proven this on the top level. And I think although he was not available in all the games, he's already on three goals, if I'm not completely wrong. There were also tight games on Premier League level and it's still early doors, just the seventh game day. I'm pretty sure they won't finish on the position where they are currently in." Farke's expectation is that Sunderland will be well up for the fight on home soil. "I also expect a team who plays also to their plans and to their DNA and also what they've done over the last seasons. Many teams found it very difficult to travel to the Stadium of Light. And we know also how difficult it is be competitive there. We had good away games over the last seasons. And we want to do the same. But we expect also a Sunderland side who will be highly motivated and will be back to their best." Some of Sunderland's difficulties this season can be attributed to injury issues and key absentees. And I think although he was not available in all the games, he's already on three goals, if I'm not completely wrong. He's also a key player for them with his physicality, with his capability to score goals and to hold the ball. Also quick with running in behind. He's definitely a really good striker and one of their main men in the offence. It's for our defensive players to be aware and to be competitive but also for our midfielders and offensive players to make sure that there's not too much service for him. And team effort is needed to stop some good players." Whoever turns out to welcome the Whites to Wearside and regardless of what the league table may suggest, Farke believes Leeds' mentality has to be spot on to get what they want from the weekend. "To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it," he said. "And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don't go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for each every point."

item.title: Lewandowski endorses Yamal for Ballon d’Or, praises Kane and Olise
item.description: Former Bayern Munich star Robert Lewandowski has offered his two cents on who he believes deserves the coveted Ballon d’Or. The Polish striker has a few names in mind, two of which hail from his former club in Munich. In an interview with The Athletic (captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Lewandowski had nothing but high praise for Lamine Yamal, Michael Olise, and Harry Kane when discussing potential winners for this year’s Ballon d’Or. He admitted he is leaning toward Lamine Yamal bagging the prize, saying, “Of course, I push my finger for Lamine to win the Ballon d’Or, because he’s amazing, especially for his age.” After endorsing his former teammate at Barcelona, he also turned his attention to Kane and Olise—two very viable contenders for the award. “Harry Kane came to Bayern in his prime, and what he’s doing is amazing—how many goals he’s scoring, and especially [the fact] that Bayern missed this kind of striker after I left. With him, they’re doing a really good job. And Olise, for me, is like: ‘Wow.’ He’s the game-changer player. And I think this work and cooperation between Kane, Olise, and Díaz is like a perfect match,” said the Polish star. He specifically praised how Bayern’s frontline has evolved, singling out the French winger as a unique, world-class talent. “And how they played last season, I think the only thing that was missing for Bayern was the Champions League trophy. If they won the Champions League last year, that probably would be [seen as] the same as the year we had in 2020, when we won everything, because they played amazing. The Bundesliga changed a bit [since] the last one or two years compared to when I was there. If you see that Bayern Munich wins against Leipzig now, 6-1, for the league maybe it’s not the perfect game. But of course, how Bayern develops, that is something amazing that everyone can learn from them [and] try to follow them,” Lewandowski said. “Olise has a huge future. I know that everyone is talking about Lamine, but I try to find sometimes the different players and see something, sometimes that not everyone sees yet. For me also, probably if [Olise] scored one or two goals in the World Cup, he would be the favorite also to win the Ballon d’Or, with Lamine or with Harry Kane, also. His decisions are perfect. He knows timing, he knows when he should shoot to score a goal, he knows when to play the pass, what kind of pass. I love to watch Lamine, but also Olise—to watch how they play.” This is high praise coming from someone who knows the ins and outs of Bayern’s offense as well as the challenges of competing in the Bundesliga and at the highest levels of Europe. The race for the Ballon d’Or is close, but statements like these can tip the scales—that is, of course, if the award hasn’t already been decided. With praise and endorsements pouring in from all directions, the expectations around Bayern’s attack have never been higher. Who do you think will win the award? Let us know in the comments!

Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. item.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. Continue reading...

item.title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs
item.description: Forward sent off after 80 minutes for second yellow card ‘We need to have maturity to deal with difficult moments’ Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’s shock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham , who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an own goal from Mike Penders and a late effort from Mathys Tel. Spurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old. Continue reading...

item.title: Why Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry Kane | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate Systems football began In 1963 (On the hallowed turf at Wembley) With the impact of a cynical foul By Gino Pivatelli. At that moment in the European Cup final, when the hard-working Milan forward, brought in to combat Benfica’s Mário Coluna, caught the great playmaker, football of the individual came to an end. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. Modern football was born. Continue reading...

Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. item.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
item.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. This story will be updated after Sunday’s matches Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
item.description: Head coach in hospital after collapsing in training Assistant coach Aaron Danks to take charge against Freiburg Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. Continue reading...

item.title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
item.description: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, José Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico. Not yet anyway, but it’s time: on Sunday night he returns to the stadium he first arrived at 30 transformative years ago as Bobby Robson’s talented young translator, and last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football. The coach who once declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and claimed he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them, has been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona. It is not the first time: if his return is about nostalgia, which it is, that’s wrapped up in their rivals too. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
item.description: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks. Continue reading...

item.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
item.description: Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer. Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
item.description: Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe
item.content:encoded: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
